In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka
The Book of Analysis
1. Analysis of the Aggregates
1. Classification According to the Discourses
There are five aggregates – the aggregate of material form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness.
1. The Aggregate of Material Form

Therein, what is the aggregate of material form? Whatever material form there is – past, future, or present; one's own or another's; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near – all of it gathered and grouped together: this is called the aggregate of material form.

Therein, what is past material form? Material form that is past, ceased, gone, changed, ended, completely ended, that arose and then disappeared, that is past and counted as belonging to the past – that is, the four great elements and the material form derived from the four great elements: this is called past material form. ⤵ Therein, what is future material form? Material form that is not yet born, not yet come to be, not yet come about, not yet produced, not yet brought forth, not yet appeared, not yet arisen, not yet come up, not yet emerged, not yet come into view, that is future and counted as belonging to the future – that is, the four great elements and the material form derived from the four great elements: this is called future material form. ⤵ Therein, what is present material form? Material form that is born, come to be, come about, produced, brought forth, appeared, arisen, come up, emerged, come into view, that is present and counted as belonging to the present – that is, the four great elements and the material form derived from the four great elements: this is called present material form.

Therein, what is one's own material form? Material form that, for this or that being, is internal, personal, one's own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, the four great elements and the material form derived from the four great elements: this is called one's own material form. ⤵ Therein, what is another's material form? Material form that, for this or that other being, this or that other person, is internal, personal, their own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, the four great elements and the material form derived from the four great elements: this is called another's material form.

Therein, what is coarse material form? The eye faculty… the sense-field of touch: this is called coarse material form. ⤵ Therein, what is subtle material form? The faculty of femininity… physical food: this is called subtle material form.

Therein, what is inferior material form? Material form that, for this or that being, is looked down on, despised, scorned, treated with contempt, disregarded, considered low, thought of as low, agreed to be low, unwanted, unattractive, disagreeable – that is, sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and things touched: this is called inferior material form. ⤵ Therein, what is superior material form? Material form that, for this or that being, is not looked down on, not despised, not scorned, not treated with contempt, but regarded highly, considered excellent, thought of as excellent, agreed to be excellent, wanted, attractive, agreeable – that is, sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and things touched: this is called superior material form. But material form should also be understood as inferior or superior only relative to this or that other material form.

Therein, what is material form that is far? The faculty of femininity… physical food; or whatever other material form there is that is not close, not nearby, far off, not near: this is called material form that is far. ⤵ Therein, what is material form that is near? The eye sense-field… the sense-field of touch; or whatever other material form there is that is close, nearby, not far off, near: this is called material form that is near. But material form should also be understood as far or near only relative to this or that other material form.
2. The Aggregate of Feeling

Therein, what is the aggregate of feeling? Whatever feeling there is – past, future, or present; one's own or another's; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near – all of it gathered and grouped together: this is called the aggregate of feeling.

Therein, what is past feeling? Feeling that is past, ceased, gone, changed, ended, completely ended, that arose and then disappeared, that is past and counted as belonging to the past – that is, pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant: this is called past feeling. ⤵ Therein, what is future feeling? Feeling that is not yet born, not yet come to be, not yet come about, not yet produced, not yet brought forth, not yet appeared, not yet arisen, not yet come up, not yet emerged, not yet come into view, that is future and counted as belonging to the future – that is, pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant: this is called future feeling. ⤵ Therein, what is present feeling? Feeling that is born, come to be, come about, produced, brought forth, appeared, arisen, come up, emerged, come into view, that is present and counted as belonging to the present – that is, pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant: this is called present feeling.

Therein, what is one's own feeling? Feeling that, for this or that being, is internal, personal, one's own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant: this is called one's own feeling. ⤵ Therein, what is another's feeling? Feeling that, for this or that other being, this or that other person, is internal, personal, their own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant: this is called another's feeling.

Therein, what is coarse feeling, and what is subtle feeling? Unwholesome feeling is coarse; wholesome and neutral feeling is subtle. Wholesome and unwholesome feeling is coarse; neutral feeling is subtle. Painful feeling is coarse; pleasant feeling and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are subtle. Pleasant and painful feeling is coarse; feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is subtle. The feeling of someone not in meditative absorption is coarse; the feeling of someone in meditative absorption is subtle. Feeling connected with the mental defilements is coarse; feeling free of the defilements is subtle. But feeling should also be understood as coarse or subtle only relative to this or that other feeling.

Therein, what is inferior feeling, and what is superior feeling? Unwholesome feeling is inferior; wholesome and neutral feeling is superior. Wholesome and unwholesome feeling is inferior; neutral feeling is superior. Painful feeling is inferior; pleasant feeling and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are superior. Pleasant and painful feeling is inferior; feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is superior. The feeling of someone not in meditative absorption is inferior; the feeling of someone in meditative absorption is superior. Feeling connected with the defilements is inferior; feeling free of the defilements is superior. But feeling should also be understood as inferior or superior only relative to this or that other feeling.

Therein, what is feeling that is far? Unwholesome feeling is far from wholesome and neutral feelings; wholesome and neutral feeling is far from unwholesome feeling; wholesome feeling is far from unwholesome and neutral feelings; unwholesome and neutral feeling is far from wholesome feeling; neutral feeling is far from wholesome and unwholesome feelings; wholesome and unwholesome feeling is far from neutral feeling. Painful feeling is far from pleasant feeling and from feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant; pleasant feeling and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are far from painful feeling; pleasant feeling is far from painful feeling and from feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant; painful feeling and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are far from pleasant feeling; feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is far from pleasant and painful feelings; pleasant and painful feeling is far from feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The feeling of someone not in meditative absorption is far from the feeling of someone in absorption; the feeling of someone in absorption is far from the feeling of someone not in absorption. Feeling connected with the defilements is far from feeling free of the defilements; feeling free of the defilements is far from feeling connected with the defilements. This is called feeling that is far. ⤵ Therein, what is feeling that is near? Unwholesome feeling is near to unwholesome feeling; wholesome feeling is near to wholesome feeling; neutral feeling is near to neutral feeling. Painful feeling is near to painful feeling; pleasant feeling is near to pleasant feeling; feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is near to feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The feeling of someone not in meditative absorption is near to the feeling of someone not in absorption; the feeling of someone in absorption is near to the feeling of someone in absorption. Feeling connected with the defilements is near to feeling connected with the defilements; feeling free of the defilements is near to feeling free of the defilements. This is called feeling that is near. But feeling should also be understood as far or near only relative to this or that other feeling.
3. The Aggregate of Perception

Therein, what is the aggregate of perception? Whatever perception there is – past, future, or present; one's own or another's; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near – all of it gathered and grouped together: this is called the aggregate of perception.

Therein, what is past perception? Perception that is past, ceased, gone, changed, ended, completely ended, that arose and then disappeared, that is past and counted as belonging to the past – that is, perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-contact: this is called past perception. ⤵ Therein, what is future perception? Perception that is not yet born, not yet come to be, not yet come about, not yet produced, not yet brought forth, not yet appeared, not yet arisen, not yet come up, not yet emerged, not yet come into view, that is future and counted as belonging to the future – that is, perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-contact: this is called future perception. ⤵ Therein, what is present perception? Perception that is born, come to be, come about, produced, brought forth, appeared, arisen, come up, emerged, come into view, that is present and counted as belonging to the present – that is, perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-contact: this is called present perception.
Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa
Abhidhammapiṭake
Vibhaṅgapāḷi
1. Khandhavibhaṅgo
1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ
Pañcakkhandhā – rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho.
1. Rūpakkhandho

Tattha katamo rūpakkhandho? Yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati rūpakkhandho.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ atītaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgataṃ uppajjitvā vigataṃ atītaṃ atītaṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ atītaṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ anāgataṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtaṃ anuppannaṃ asamuppannaṃ anuṭṭhitaṃ asamuṭṭhitaṃ anāgataṃ anāgataṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ anāgataṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ paccuppannaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ sañjātaṃ nibbattaṃ abhinibbattaṃ pātubhūtaṃ uppannaṃ samuppannaṃ uṭṭhitaṃ samuṭṭhitaṃ paccuppannaṃ paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ paccuppannaṃ.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ upādinnaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ ajjhattaṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ bahiddhā? Yaṃ rūpaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ upādinnaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ bahiddhā.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ oḷārikaṃ? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ oḷārikaṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ sukhumaṃ? Itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro [kabaḷiṃkāro (sī. syā.)] āhāro – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ sukhumaṃ.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ hīnaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ uññātaṃ avaññātaṃ hīḷitaṃ paribhūtaṃ acittīkataṃ hīnaṃ hīnamataṃ hīnasammataṃ aniṭṭhaṃ akantaṃ amanāpaṃ, rūpā saddā gandhā rasā phoṭṭhabbā – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ hīnaṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ paṇītaṃ? Yaṃ rūpaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ anuññātaṃ anavaññātaṃ ahīḷitaṃ aparibhūtaṃ cittīkataṃ paṇītaṃ paṇītamataṃ paṇītasammataṃ iṭṭhaṃ kantaṃ manāpaṃ, rūpā saddā gandhā rasā phoṭṭhabbā – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ paṇītaṃ. Taṃ taṃ vā pana rūpaṃ upādāyupādāya rūpaṃ hīnaṃ paṇītaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ dūre? Itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ anāsanne anupakaṭṭhe dūre asantike – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ dūre. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ santike? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi rūpaṃ āsanne upakaṭṭhe avidūre santike – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ santike. Taṃ taṃ vā pana rūpaṃ upādāyupādāya rūpaṃ dūre santike daṭṭhabbaṃ.
2. Vedanākkhandho

Tattha katamo vedanākkhandho? Yā kāci vedanā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā yā dūre santike vā, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanākkhandho.

Tattha katamā vedanā atītā? Yā vedanā atītā niruddhā vigatā vipariṇatā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā uppajjitvā vigatā atītā atītaṃsena saṅgahitā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā atītā. ⤵ Tattha katamā vedanā anāgatā? Yā vedanā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anāgatā anāgataṃsena saṅgahitā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā anāgatā. ⤵ Tattha katamā vedanā paccuppannā? Yā vedanā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā paccuppannā paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā paccuppannā.

Tattha katamā vedanā ajjhattā? Yā vedanā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā ajjhattā. ⤵ Tattha katamā vedanā bahiddhā? Yā vedanā tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, sukhā vedanā dukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā bahiddhā.

Tattha katamā vedanā oḷārikā sukhumā? Akusalā vedanā oḷārikā, kusalābyākatā vedanā sukhumā. Kusalākusalā vedanā oḷārikā, abyākatā vedanā sukhumā. Dukkhā vedanā oḷārikā, sukhā ca adukkhamasukhā ca vedanā sukhumā. Sukhadukkhā vedanā oḷārikā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā sukhumā. Asamāpannassa vedanā oḷārikā, samāpannassa vedanā sukhumā. Sāsavā vedanā oḷārikā, anāsavā vedanā sukhumā. Taṃ taṃ vā pana vedanaṃ upādāyupādāya vedanā oḷārikā sukhumā daṭṭhabbā.

Tattha katamā vedanā hīnā paṇītā? Akusalā vedanā hīnā, kusalābyākatā vedanā paṇītā. Kusalākusalā vedanā hīnā, abyākatā vedanā paṇītā. Dukkhā vedanā hīnā, sukhā ca adukkhamasukhā ca vedanā paṇītā. Sukhadukkhā vedanā hīnā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā paṇītā. Asamāpannassa vedanā hīnā, samāpannassa vedanā paṇītā. Sāsavā vedanā hīnā, anāsavā vedanā paṇītā. Taṃ taṃ vā pana vedanaṃ upādāyupādāya vedanā hīnā paṇītā daṭṭhabbā.

Tattha katamā vedanā dūre? Akusalā vedanā kusalābyākatāhi vedanāhi dūre; kusalābyākatā vedanā akusalāya vedanāya dūre; kusalā vedanā akusalābyākatāhi vedanāhi dūre; akusalābyākatā vedanā kusalāya vedanāya dūre; abyākatā vedanā kusalākusalāhi vedanāhi dūre; kusalākusalā vedanā abyākatāya vedanāya dūre. Dukkhā vedanā sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi dūre; sukhā ca adukkhamasukhā ca vedanā dukkhāya vedanāya dūre; sukhā vedanā dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi dūre; dukkhā ca adukkhamasukhā ca vedanā sukhāya vedanāya dūre; adukkhamasukhā vedanā sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi dūre; sukhadukkhā vedanā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya dūre. Asamāpannassa vedanā samāpannassa vedanāya dūre; samāpannassa vedanā asamāpannassa vedanāya dūre. Sāsavā vedanā anāsavāya vedanāya dūre; anāsavā vedanā sāsavāya vedanāya dūre – ayaṃ vuccati vedanā dūre. ⤵ Tattha katamā vedanā santike? Akusalā vedanā akusalāya vedanāya santike; kusalā vedanā kusalāya vedanāya santike; abyākatā vedanā abyākatāya vedanāya santike. Dukkhā vedanā dukkhāya vedanāya santike; sukhā vedanā sukhāya vedanāya santike; adukkhamasukhā vedanā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya santike . Asamāpannassa vedanā asamāpannassa vedanāya santike; samāpannassa vedanā samāpannassa vedanāya santike. Sāsavā vedanā sāsavāya vedanāya santike; anāsavā vedanā anāsavāya vedanāya santike. Ayaṃ vuccati vedanā santike. Taṃ taṃ vā pana vedanaṃ upādāyupādāya vedanā dūre santike daṭṭhabbā.
3. Saññākkhandho

Tattha katamo saññākkhandho? Yā kāci saññā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā yā dūre santike vā tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati saññākkhandho.

Tattha katamā saññā atītā? Yā saññā atītā niruddhā vigatā vipariṇatā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā uppajjitvā vigatā atītā atītaṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā atītā. ⤵ Tattha katamā saññā anāgatā? Yā saññā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anāgatā anāgataṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā anāgatā. ⤵ Tattha katamā saññā paccuppannā? Yā saññā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā paccuppannā paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā paccuppannā.

Therein, what is one's own perception? Perception that, for this or that being, is internal, personal, one's own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-contact: this is called one's own perception. ⤵ Therein, what is another's perception? Perception that, for this or that other being, this or that other person, is internal, personal, their own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-contact: this is called another's perception.

Therein, what is coarse perception, and what is subtle perception? Perception born of sense-impact is coarse; perception born of naming is subtle. Unwholesome perception is coarse; wholesome and neutral perception is subtle. Wholesome and unwholesome perception is coarse; neutral perception is subtle. Perception joined with painful feeling is coarse; perception joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is subtle. Perception joined with pleasant and painful feelings is coarse; perception joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is subtle. The perception of someone not in meditative absorption is coarse; the perception of someone in meditative absorption is subtle. Perception connected with the defilements is coarse; perception free of the defilements is subtle. But perception should also be understood as coarse or subtle only relative to this or that other perception.

Therein, what is inferior perception, and what is superior perception? Unwholesome perception is inferior; wholesome and neutral perception is superior. Wholesome and unwholesome perception is inferior; neutral perception is superior. Perception joined with painful feeling is inferior; perception joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is superior. Perception joined with pleasant and painful feelings is inferior; perception joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is superior. The perception of someone not in meditative absorption is inferior; the perception of someone in meditative absorption is superior. Perception connected with the defilements is inferior; perception free of the defilements is superior. But perception should also be understood as inferior or superior only relative to this or that other perception.

Therein, what is perception that is far? Unwholesome perception is far from wholesome and neutral perceptions; wholesome and neutral perception is far from unwholesome perception; wholesome perception is far from unwholesome and neutral perceptions; unwholesome and neutral perception is far from wholesome perception. Neutral perception is far from wholesome and unwholesome perceptions; wholesome and unwholesome perception is far from neutral perception. Perception joined with painful feeling is far from perceptions joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant; perception joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is far from perception joined with painful feeling; perception joined with pleasant feeling is far from perceptions joined with painful feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant; perception joined with painful feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is far from perception joined with pleasant feeling; perception joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is far from perceptions joined with pleasant and painful feelings; perception joined with pleasant and painful feelings is far from perception joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The perception of someone not in meditative absorption is far from the perception of someone in absorption; the perception of someone in absorption is far from the perception of someone not in absorption. Perception connected with the defilements is far from perception free of the defilements; perception free of the defilements is far from perception connected with the defilements. This is called perception that is far. ⤵ Therein, what is perception that is near? Unwholesome perception is near to unwholesome perception; wholesome perception is near to wholesome perception; neutral perception is near to neutral perception. Perception joined with painful feeling is near to perception joined with painful feeling; perception joined with pleasant feeling is near to perception joined with pleasant feeling; perception joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is near to perception joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The perception of someone not in meditative absorption is near to the perception of someone not in absorption; the perception of someone in absorption is near to the perception of someone in absorption. Perception connected with the defilements is near to perception connected with the defilements; perception free of the defilements is near to perception free of the defilements. This is called perception that is near. But perception should also be understood as far or near only relative to this or that other perception.
4. The Aggregate of Mental Formations

Therein, what is the aggregate of mental formations? Whatever mental formations there are – past, future, or present; one's own or another's; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near – all of them gathered and grouped together: this is called the aggregate of mental formations.

Therein, what are past mental formations? Mental formations that are past, ceased, gone, changed, ended, completely ended, that arose and then disappeared, that are past and counted as belonging to the past – that is, intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, intention born of mind-contact: these are called past mental formations. ⤵ Therein, what are future mental formations? Mental formations that are not yet born, not yet come to be, not yet come about, not yet produced, not yet brought forth, not yet appeared, not yet arisen, not yet come up, not yet emerged, not yet come into view, that are future and counted as belonging to the future – that is, intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, intention born of mind-contact: these are called future mental formations. ⤵ Therein, what are present mental formations? Mental formations that are born, come to be, come about, produced, brought forth, appeared, arisen, come up, emerged, come into view, that are present and counted as belonging to the present – that is, intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, intention born of mind-contact: these are called present mental formations.

Therein, what are one's own mental formations? Mental formations that, for this or that being, are internal, personal, one's own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, intention born of mind-contact: these are called one's own mental formations. ⤵ Therein, what are another's mental formations? Mental formations that, for this or that other being, this or that other person, are internal, personal, their own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, intention born of mind-contact: these are called another's mental formations.

Therein, what are coarse mental formations, and what are subtle ones? Unwholesome formations are coarse; wholesome and neutral formations are subtle. Wholesome and unwholesome formations are coarse; neutral formations are subtle. Formations joined with painful feeling are coarse; formations joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are subtle. Formations joined with pleasant and painful feelings are coarse; formations joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are subtle. The formations of someone not in meditative absorption are coarse; the formations of someone in meditative absorption are subtle. Formations connected with the defilements are coarse; formations free of the defilements are subtle. But mental formations should also be understood as coarse or subtle only relative to these or those other formations.

Therein, what are inferior mental formations, and what are superior ones? Unwholesome formations are inferior; wholesome and neutral formations are superior. Wholesome and unwholesome formations are inferior; neutral formations are superior. Formations joined with painful feeling are inferior; formations joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are superior. Formations joined with pleasant and painful feelings are inferior; formations joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are superior. The formations of someone not in meditative absorption are inferior; the formations of someone in meditative absorption are superior. Formations connected with the defilements are inferior; formations free of the defilements are superior. But mental formations should also be understood as inferior or superior only relative to these or those other formations.

Therein, what are mental formations that are far? Unwholesome formations are far from wholesome and neutral formations; wholesome and neutral formations are far from unwholesome formations; wholesome formations are far from unwholesome and neutral formations; unwholesome and neutral formations are far from wholesome formations; neutral formations are far from wholesome and unwholesome formations; wholesome and unwholesome formations are far from neutral formations. Formations joined with painful feeling are far from formations joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant; formations joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are far from formations joined with painful feeling; formations joined with pleasant feeling are far from formations joined with painful feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant; formations joined with painful feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are far from formations joined with pleasant feeling; formations joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are far from formations joined with pleasant and painful feelings; formations joined with pleasant and painful feelings are far from formations joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The formations of someone not in meditative absorption are far from the formations of someone in absorption; the formations of someone in absorption are far from the formations of someone not in absorption. Formations connected with the defilements are far from formations free of the defilements; formations free of the defilements are far from formations connected with the defilements. These are called mental formations that are far. ⤵ Therein, what are mental formations that are near? Unwholesome formations are near to unwholesome formations; wholesome formations are near to wholesome formations; neutral formations are near to neutral formations. Formations joined with painful feeling are near to formations joined with painful feeling; formations joined with pleasant feeling are near to formations joined with pleasant feeling; formations joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant are near to formations joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The formations of someone not in meditative absorption are near to the formations of someone not in absorption; the formations of someone in absorption are near to the formations of someone in absorption. Formations connected with the defilements are near to formations connected with the defilements; formations free of the defilements are near to formations free of the defilements. These are called mental formations that are near. But mental formations should also be understood as far or near only relative to these or those other formations.

Tattha katamā saññā ajjhattā? Yā saññā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā ajjhattā. ⤵ Tattha katamā saññā bahiddhā? Yā saññā tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, cakkhusamphassajā saññā sotasamphassajā saññā ghānasamphassajā saññā jivhāsamphassajā saññā kāyasamphassajā saññā manosamphassajā saññā – ayaṃ vuccati saññā bahiddhā.

Tattha katamā saññā oḷārikā sukhumā? Paṭighasamphassajā saññā oḷārikā, adhivacanasamphassajā saññā sukhumā. Akusalā saññā oḷārikā, kusalābyākatā saññā sukhumā. Kusalākusalā saññā oḷārikā, abyākatā saññā sukhumā. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā oḷārikā, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā sukhumā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā oḷārikā , adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā sukhumā. Asamāpannassa saññā oḷārikā, samāpannassa saññā sukhumā. Sāsavā saññā oḷārikā, anāsavā saññā sukhumā. Taṃ taṃ vā pana saññaṃ upādāyupādāya saññā oḷārikā sukhumā daṭṭhabbā.

Tattha katamā saññā hīnā paṇītā? Akusalā saññā hīnā, kusalābyākatā saññā paṇītā. Kusalākusalā saññā hīnā, abyākatā saññā paṇītā. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā hīnā, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā paṇītā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā hīnā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā paṇītā. Asamāpannassa saññā hīnā, samāpannassa saññā paṇītā. Sāsavā saññā hīnā, anāsavā saññā paṇītā. Taṃ taṃ vā pana saññaṃ upādāyupādāya saññā hīnā paṇītā daṭṭhabbā.

Tattha katamā saññā dūre? Akusalā saññā kusalābyākatāhi saññāhi dūre; kusalābyākatā saññā akusalāya saññāya dūre; kusalā saññā akusalābyākatāhi saññāhi dūre; akusalābyākatā saññā kusalāya saññāya dūre. Abyākatā saññā kusalākusalāhi saññāhi dūre; kusalākusalā saññā abyākatāya saññāya dūre. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttāhi saññāhi dūre; sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya dūre; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttāhi saññāhi dūre; dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya dūre; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttāhi saññāhi dūre; sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saññā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya dūre. Asamāpannassa saññā samāpannassa saññāya dūre; samāpannassa saññā asamāpannassa saññāya dūre. Sāsavā saññā anāsavāya saññāya dūre; anāsavā saññā sāsavāya saññāya dūre – ayaṃ vuccati saññā dūre. ⤵ Tattha katamā saññā santike? Akusalā saññā akusalāya saññāya santike; kusalā saññā kusalāya saññāya santike; abyākatā saññā abyākatāya saññāya santike. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya santike; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya santike; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saññā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttāya saññāya santike. Asamāpannassa saññā asamāpannassa saññāya santike; samāpannassa saññā samāpannassa saññāya santike. Sāsavā saññā sāsavāya saññāya santike; anāsavā saññā anāsavāya saññāya santike. Ayaṃ vuccati saññā santike. Taṃ taṃ vā pana saññaṃ upādāyupādāya saññā dūre santike daṭṭhabbā.
4. Saṅkhārakkhandho

Tattha katamo saṅkhārakkhandho? Ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā ye dūre santike vā, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati saṅkhārakkhandho.

Tattha katame saṅkhārā atītā? Ye saṅkhārā atītā niruddhā vigatā vipariṇatā atthaṅgatā abbhatthaṅgatā uppajjitvā vigatā atītā atītaṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā atītā. ⤵ Tattha katame saṅkhārā anāgatā? Ye saṅkhārā ajātā abhūtā asañjātā anibbattā anabhinibbattā apātubhūtā anuppannā asamuppannā anuṭṭhitā asamuṭṭhitā anāgatā anāgataṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā anāgatā. ⤵ Tattha katame saṅkhārā paccuppannā? Ye saṅkhārā jātā bhūtā sañjātā nibbattā abhinibbattā pātubhūtā uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā paccuppannā paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā paccuppannā.

Tattha katame saṅkhārā ajjhattā? Ye saṅkhārā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā ajjhattā. ⤵ Tattha katame saṅkhārā bahiddhā? Ye saṅkhārā tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakā pāṭipuggalikā upādinnā, cakkhusamphassajā cetanā sotasamphassajā cetanā ghānasamphassajā cetanā jivhāsamphassajā cetanā kāyasamphassajā cetanā manosamphassajā cetanā – ime vuccanti saṅkhārā bahiddhā.

Tattha katame saṅkhārā oḷārikā sukhumā? Akusalā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, kusalābyākatā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Kusalākusalā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, abyākatā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Asamāpannassa saṅkhārā oḷārikā, samāpannassa saṅkhārā sukhumā. Sāsavā saṅkhārā oḷārikā, anāsavā saṅkhārā sukhumā. Te te vā pana saṅkhāre upādāyupādāya saṅkhārā oḷārikā sukhumā daṭṭhabbā.

Tattha katame saṅkhārā hīnā paṇītā? Akusalā saṅkhārā hīnā, kusalābyākatā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Kusalākusalā saṅkhārā hīnā, abyākatā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā hīnā , sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā hīnā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Asamāpannassa saṅkhārā hīnā, samāpannassa saṅkhārā paṇītā. Sāsavā saṅkhārā hīnā, anāsavā saṅkhārā paṇītā. Te te vā pana saṅkhāre upādāyupādāya saṅkhārā hīnā paṇītā daṭṭhabbā.

Tattha katame saṅkhārā dūre? Akusalā saṅkhārā kusalābyākatehi saṅkhārehi dūre; kusalābyākatā saṅkhārā akusalehi saṅkhārehi dūre; kusalā saṅkhārā akusalābyākatehi saṅkhārehi dūre; akusalābyākatā saṅkhārā kusalehi saṅkhārehi dūre; abyākatā saṅkhārā kusalākusalehi saṅkhārehi dūre; kusalākusalā saṅkhārā abyākatehi saṅkhārehi dūre. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre; sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā saṅkhārā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttehi saṅkhārehi dūre . Asamāpannassa saṅkhārā samāpannassa saṅkhārehi dūre; samāpannassa saṅkhārā asamāpannassa saṅkhārehi dūre. Sāsavā saṅkhārā anāsavehi saṅkhārehi dūre; anāsavā saṅkhārā sāsavehi saṅkhārehi dūre. Ime vuccanti saṅkhārā dūre. ⤵ Tattha katame saṅkhārā santike? Akusalā saṅkhārā akusalānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; kusalā saṅkhārā kusalānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; abyākatā saṅkhārā abyākatānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā saṅkhārā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike. Asamāpannassa saṅkhārā asamāpannassa saṅkhārānaṃ santike; samāpannassa saṅkhārā samāpannassa saṅkhārānaṃ santike. Sāsavā saṅkhārā sāsavānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike; anāsavā saṅkhārā anāsavānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ santike. Ime vuccanti saṅkhārā santike. Te te vā pana saṅkhāre upādāyupādāya saṅkhārā dūre santike daṭṭhabbā.
5. The Aggregate of Consciousness

Therein, what is the aggregate of consciousness? Whatever consciousness there is – past, future, or present; one's own or another's; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near – all of it gathered and grouped together: this is called the aggregate of consciousness.

Therein, what is past consciousness? Consciousness that is past, ceased, gone, changed, ended, completely ended, that arose and then disappeared, that is past and counted as belonging to the past – that is, eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called past consciousness. ⤵ Therein, what is future consciousness? Consciousness that is not yet born, not yet come to be, not yet come about, not yet produced, not yet brought forth, not yet appeared, not yet arisen, not yet come up, not yet emerged, not yet come into view, that is future and counted as belonging to the future – that is, eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called future consciousness. ⤵ Therein, what is present consciousness? Consciousness that is born, come to be, come about, produced, brought forth, appeared, arisen, come up, emerged, come into view, that is present and counted as belonging to the present – that is, eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called present consciousness.

Therein, what is one's own consciousness? Consciousness that, for this or that being, is internal, personal, one's own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called one's own consciousness. ⤵ Therein, what is another's consciousness? Consciousness that, for this or that other being, this or that other person, is internal, personal, their own, individual, and taken up at birth – that is, eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called another's consciousness.

Therein, what is coarse consciousness, and what is subtle consciousness? Unwholesome consciousness is coarse; wholesome and neutral consciousness is subtle. Wholesome and unwholesome consciousness is coarse; neutral consciousness is subtle. Consciousness joined with painful feeling is coarse; consciousness joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is subtle. Consciousness joined with pleasant and painful feelings is coarse; consciousness joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is subtle. The consciousness of someone not in meditative absorption is coarse; the consciousness of someone in meditative absorption is subtle. Consciousness connected with the defilements is coarse; consciousness free of the defilements is subtle. But consciousness should also be understood as coarse or subtle only relative to this or that other consciousness.

Therein, what is inferior consciousness, and what is superior consciousness? Unwholesome consciousness is inferior; wholesome and neutral consciousness is superior. Wholesome and unwholesome consciousness is inferior; neutral consciousness is superior. Consciousness joined with painful feeling is inferior; consciousness joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is superior. Consciousness joined with pleasant and painful feelings is inferior; consciousness joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is superior. The consciousness of someone not in meditative absorption is inferior; the consciousness of someone in meditative absorption is superior. Consciousness connected with the defilements is inferior; consciousness free of the defilements is superior. But consciousness should also be understood as inferior or superior only relative to this or that other consciousness.

Therein, what is consciousness that is far? Unwholesome consciousness is far from wholesome and neutral consciousness; wholesome and neutral consciousness is far from unwholesome consciousness; wholesome consciousness is far from unwholesome and neutral consciousness; unwholesome and neutral consciousness is far from wholesome consciousness; neutral consciousness is far from wholesome and unwholesome consciousness; wholesome and unwholesome consciousness is far from neutral consciousness. Consciousness joined with painful feeling is far from consciousness joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant; consciousness joined with pleasant feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is far from consciousness joined with painful feeling; consciousness joined with pleasant feeling is far from consciousness joined with painful feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant; consciousness joined with painful feeling and with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is far from consciousness joined with pleasant feeling; consciousness joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is far from consciousness joined with pleasant and painful feelings; consciousness joined with pleasant and painful feelings is far from consciousness joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The consciousness of someone not in meditative absorption is far from the consciousness of someone in absorption; the consciousness of someone in absorption is far from the consciousness of someone not in absorption. Consciousness connected with the defilements is far from consciousness free of the defilements; consciousness free of the defilements is far from consciousness connected with the defilements. This is called consciousness that is far. ⤵ Therein, what is consciousness that is near? Unwholesome consciousness is near to unwholesome consciousness; wholesome consciousness is near to wholesome consciousness; neutral consciousness is near to neutral consciousness. Consciousness joined with painful feeling is near to consciousness joined with painful feeling; consciousness joined with pleasant feeling is near to consciousness joined with pleasant feeling; consciousness joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant is near to consciousness joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The consciousness of someone not in meditative absorption is near to the consciousness of someone not in absorption; the consciousness of someone in absorption is near to the consciousness of someone in absorption. Consciousness connected with the defilements is near to consciousness connected with the defilements; consciousness free of the defilements is near to consciousness free of the defilements. This is called consciousness that is near. But consciousness should also be understood as far or near only relative to this or that other consciousness.
The Classification According to the Discourses is finished.
2. Classification According to the Abhidhamma
There are five aggregates – the aggregate of material form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness.
1. The Aggregate of Material Form

Therein, what is the aggregate of material form? As a single class, the aggregate of material form is this: all material form is not a root cause, is without root causes, is dissociated from root causes; it exists with conditions, is compounded, is material; it is worldly, subject to the mental taints, able to bind with the fetters, able to tie with the ties, able to sweep away with the floods, able to yoke with the yokes, able to obstruct with the hindrances, able to be wrongly grasped, able to be clung to, open to defilement; it is neutral, without an object, not a mental factor, dissociated from mind; it is neither a result nor something that produces results; it is undefiled yet open to defilement; it is not accompanied by both thought and examination, not accompanied by examination alone, but without both thought and examination; it is not accompanied by joy, not accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by equanimity; it is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development, and its root causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development; it neither leads to further accumulation nor to dismantling; it belongs neither to trainees nor to those beyond training; it is limited, belongs to the sense sphere, does not belong to the fine-material sphere, does not belong to the immaterial sphere; it is included in the round of existence, not outside it; it is not fixed in its outcome, does not lead out of the round; it is arisen, and can be known by the six kinds of consciousness; it is impermanent and overcome by aging. This is the aggregate of material form as a single class. ⤵ As a twofold class, the aggregate of material form is this: there is material form that is derived, and material form that is not derived. There is material form that is taken up at birth, and material form that is not. There is material form that is taken up and can be clung to, and material form that is not taken up but can be clung to. There is material form that is visible, and material form that is invisible. There is material form that offers resistance, and material form that does not. There is material form that is a faculty, and material form that is not. There is material form that is a great element, and material form that is not. There is material form that is bodily or verbal expression, and material form that is not. There is material form produced by mind, and material form not produced by mind. There is material form that arises together with mind, and material form that does not. There is material form that follows along with mind, and material form that does not. There is material form that is internal, and material form that is external. There is material form that is coarse, and material form that is subtle. There is material form that is far, and material form that is near… there is material form that is physical food, and material form that is not physical food. This is the aggregate of material form as a twofold class. ⤵ (As this was analysed in the Chapter on Material Form, so it should be analysed here.) ⤵ As a threefold class, the aggregate of material form is this: material form that is internal is derived; material form that is external may be derived or not derived. Material form that is internal is taken up at birth; material form that is external may be taken up or not taken up. Material form that is internal is taken up and can be clung to; material form that is external may be taken up and clung to, or not taken up but able to be clung to… material form that is internal is not physical food; material form that is external may be physical food or not physical food. This is the aggregate of material form as a threefold class. ⤵ As a fourfold class, the aggregate of material form is this: material form that is derived may be taken up at birth or not taken up; material form that is not derived may be taken up or not taken up. Material form that is derived may be taken up and clung to, or not taken up but able to be clung to; material form that is not derived may be taken up and clung to, or not taken up but able to be clung to. Material form that is derived may offer resistance or not; material form that is not derived may offer resistance or not. Material form that is derived may be coarse or subtle; material form that is not derived may be coarse or subtle. Material form that is derived may be far or near; material form that is not derived may be far or near… and there is material form that is seen, heard, sensed, and cognized. This is the aggregate of material form as a fourfold class. ⤵ As a fivefold class, the aggregate of material form is this: the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the air element, and the material form derived from them. This is the aggregate of material form as a fivefold class. ⤵ As a sixfold class, the aggregate of material form is this: material form knowable by the eye, knowable by the ear, knowable by the nose, knowable by the tongue, knowable by the body, and knowable by the mind. This is the aggregate of material form as a sixfold class. ⤵ As a sevenfold class, the aggregate of material form is this: material form knowable by the eye, knowable by the ear, knowable by the nose, knowable by the tongue, knowable by the body, knowable by the mind element, and knowable by the mind-consciousness element. This is the aggregate of material form as a sevenfold class. ⤵ As an eightfold class, the aggregate of material form is this: material form knowable by the eye, knowable by the ear, knowable by the nose, knowable by the tongue, knowable by the body – which may bring pleasant contact or painful contact – knowable by the mind element, and knowable by the mind-consciousness element. This is the aggregate of material form as an eightfold class. ⤵ As a ninefold class, the aggregate of material form is this: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity, the life faculty, and material form that is not a faculty. This is the aggregate of material form as a ninefold class. ⤵ As a tenfold class, the aggregate of material form is this: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity, the life faculty, and material form that is not a faculty – which may offer resistance or not. This is the aggregate of material form as a tenfold class. ⤵ As an elevenfold class, the aggregate of material form is this: the eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the sense-field of sights, the sense-field of sounds, the sense-field of smells, the sense-field of tastes, the sense-field of things touched, and the material form that is invisible, without resistance, and included in the sense-field of mental objects. This is the aggregate of material form as an elevenfold class.
This is called the aggregate of material form.
5. Viññāṇakkhandho

Tattha katamo viññāṇakkhandho? Yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati viññāṇakkhandho.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītaṃ? Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgataṃ uppajjitvā vigataṃ atītaṃ atītaṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ atītaṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ anāgataṃ? Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtaṃ anuppannaṃ asamuppannaṃ anuṭṭhitaṃ asamuṭṭhitaṃ anāgataṃ anāgataṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ anāgataṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ paccuppannaṃ? Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ sañjātaṃ nibbattaṃ abhinibbattaṃ pātubhūtaṃ uppannaṃ samuppannaṃ uṭṭhitaṃ samuṭṭhitaṃ paccuppannaṃ paccuppannaṃsena saṅgahitaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ paccuppannaṃ.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ ajjhattaṃ? Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ upādinnaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ ajjhattaṃ. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ bahiddhā? Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ niyakaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ upādinnaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ bahiddhā.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ sukhumaṃ? Akusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ, kusalābyākatā viññāṇā sukhumā. Kusalākusalā viññāṇā oḷārikā , abyākataṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhumaṃ. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā sukhumā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā oḷārikā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhumaṃ. Asamāpannassa viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ, samāpannassa viññāṇaṃ sukhumaṃ. Sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ, anāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhumaṃ. Taṃ taṃ vā pana viññāṇaṃ upādāyupādāya viññāṇaṃ oḷārikaṃ sukhumaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ paṇītaṃ? Akusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ, kusalābyākatā viññāṇā paṇītā . Kusalākusalā viññāṇā hīnā, abyākataṃ viññāṇaṃ paṇītaṃ. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ, sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā paṇītā. Sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā hīnā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ paṇītaṃ. Asamāpannassa viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ, samāpannassa viññāṇaṃ paṇītaṃ. Sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ, anāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ paṇītaṃ. Taṃ taṃ vā pana viññāṇaṃ upādāyupādāya viññāṇaṃ hīnaṃ paṇītaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ dūre? Akusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ kusalābyākatehi viññāṇehi dūre; kusalābyākatā viññāṇā akusalā viññāṇā dūre; kusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ akusalābyākatehi viññāṇehi dūre; akusalābyākatā viññāṇā kusalā viññāṇā dūre; abyākataṃ viññāṇaṃ kusalākusalehi viññāṇehi dūre; kusalākusalā viññāṇā abyākatā viññāṇā dūre. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttehi viññāṇehi dūre; sukhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā viññāṇā dūre; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttehi viññāṇehi dūre; dukkhāya ca adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā viññāṇā dūre; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttehi viññāṇehi dūre; sukhadukkhāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā viññāṇā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā viññāṇā dūre. Asamāpannassa viññāṇaṃ samāpannassa viññāṇā dūre; samāpannassa viññāṇaṃ asamāpannassa viññāṇā dūre. Sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ anāsavā viññāṇā dūre; anāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ sāsavā viññāṇā dūre – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ dūre. ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ viññāṇaṃ santike? Akusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ akusalassa viññāṇassa santike; kusalaṃ viññāṇaṃ kusalassa viññāṇassa santike; abyākataṃ viññāṇaṃ abyākatassa viññāṇassa santike. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa viññāṇassa santike; sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa viññāṇassa santike; adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ viññāṇaṃ adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa viññāṇassa santike. Asamāpannassa viññāṇaṃ asamāpannassa viññāṇassa santike; samāpannassa viññāṇaṃ samāpannassa viññāṇassa santike. Sāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ sāsavassa viññāṇassa santike; anāsavaṃ viññāṇaṃ anāsavassa viññāṇassa santike – idaṃ vuccati viññāṇaṃ santike. Taṃ taṃ vā pana viññāṇaṃ upādāyupādāya viññāṇaṃ dūre santike daṭṭhabbaṃ.
Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.
2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ
Pañcakkhandhā – rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho.
1. Rūpakkhandho

Tattha katamo rūpakkhandho? Ekavidhena rūpakkhandho – sabbaṃ rūpaṃ na hetu, ahetukaṃ, hetuvippayuttaṃ, sappaccayaṃ, saṅkhataṃ, rūpaṃ, lokiyaṃ, sāsavaṃ, saṃyojaniyaṃ, ganthaniyaṃ, oghaniyaṃ, yoganiyaṃ, nīvaraṇiyaṃ, parāmaṭṭhaṃ, upādāniyaṃ, saṃkilesikaṃ, abyākataṃ, anārammaṇaṃ, acetasikaṃ, cittavippayuttaṃ, nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammaṃ, asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikaṃ, na savitakkasavicāraṃ, na avitakkavicāramattaṃ, avitakkaavicāraṃ, na pītisahagataṃ, na sukhasahagataṃ, na upekkhāsahagataṃ, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ, nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī, nevasekkhanāsekkhaṃ, parittaṃ, kāmāvacaraṃ, na rūpāvacaraṃ, na arūpāvacaraṃ, pariyāpannaṃ, no apariyāpannaṃ, aniyataṃ, aniyyānikaṃ, uppannaṃ, chahi viññāṇehi viññeyyaṃ, aniccaṃ, jarābhibhūtaṃ. Evaṃ ekavidhena rūpakkhandho. ⤵ Duvidhena rūpakkhandho – atthi rūpaṃ upādā, atthi rūpaṃ no upādā [nupādā (sī. ka.)]. Atthi rūpaṃ upādinnaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ anupādinnaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ upādinnupādāniyaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ sanidassanaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ sappaṭighaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ appaṭighaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ indriyaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ mahābhūtaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ na mahābhūtaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ viññatti, atthi rūpaṃ na viññatti. Atthi rūpaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ na cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ cittasahabhu, atthi rūpaṃ na cittasahabhu. Atthi rūpaṃ cittānuparivatti, atthi rūpaṃ na cittānuparivatti. Atthi rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ oḷārikaṃ, atthi rūpaṃ sukhumaṃ. Atthi rūpaṃ dūre, atthi rūpaṃ santike…pe… atthi rūpaṃ kabaḷīkāro āhāro, atthi rūpaṃ na kabaḷīkāro āhāro. Evaṃ duvidhena rūpakkhandho. ⤵ (Yathā rūpakaṇḍe vibhattaṃ, tathā idha vibhajitabbaṃ.) ⤵ Tividhena rūpakkhandho – yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ taṃ upādā, yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ taṃ atthi upādā, atthi no upādā. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ taṃ upādinnaṃ, yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ taṃ atthi upādinnaṃ, atthi anupādinnaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ taṃ upādinnupādāniyaṃ, yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ taṃ atthi upādinnupādāniyaṃ, atthi anupādinnupādāniyaṃ…pe… yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ ajjhattikaṃ taṃ na kabaḷīkāro āhāro, yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ bāhiraṃ taṃ atthi kabaḷīkāro āhāro, atthi na kabaḷīkāro āhāro. Evaṃ tividhena rūpakkhandho. ⤵ Catubbidhena rūpakkhandho – yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi upādinnaṃ, atthi anupādinnaṃ; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi upādinnaṃ, atthi anupādinnaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi upādinnupādāniyaṃ, atthi anupādinnupādāniyaṃ; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi upādinnupādāniyaṃ, atthi anupādinnupādāniyaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi sappaṭighaṃ, atthi appaṭighaṃ; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi sappaṭighaṃ, atthi appaṭighaṃ . Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi oḷārikaṃ, atthi sukhumaṃ; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi oḷārikaṃ, atthi sukhumaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ upādā taṃ atthi dūre, atthi santike; yaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ no upādā taṃ atthi dūre, atthi santike…pe… diṭṭhaṃ, sutaṃ, mutaṃ, viññātaṃ rūpaṃ. Evaṃ catubbidhena rūpakkhandho. ⤵ Pañcavidhena rūpakkhandho – pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu, yañca rūpaṃ upādā. Evaṃ pañcavidhena rūpakkhandho. ⤵ Chabbidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, sotaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, ghānaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, jivhāviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, kāyaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, manoviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ. Evaṃ chabbidhena rūpakkhandho. ⤵ Sattavidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, sotaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, ghānaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, jivhāviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, kāyaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, manodhātuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, manoviññāṇadhātuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ. Evaṃ sattavidhena rūpakkhandho . ⤵ Aṭṭhavidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, sotaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, ghānaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, jivhāviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, kāyaviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ atthi sukhasamphassaṃ, atthi dukkhasamphassaṃ, manodhātuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ, manoviññāṇadhātuviññeyyaṃ rūpaṃ. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena rūpakkhandho. ⤵ Navavidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, itthindriyaṃ, purisindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, yañca rūpaṃ na indriyaṃ. Evaṃ navavidhena rūpakkhandho. ⤵ Dasavidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, itthindriyaṃ, purisindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, na indriyaṃ rūpaṃ atthi sappaṭighaṃ, atthi appaṭighaṃ. Evaṃ dasavidhena rūpakkhandho. ⤵ Ekādasavidhena rūpakkhandho – cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ. Evaṃ ekādasavidhena rūpakkhandho.
Ayaṃ vuccati rūpakkhandho.
2. The Aggregate of Feeling

Therein, what is the aggregate of feeling? As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling with a root cause, and feeling without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, and neutral feeling. ⤵ As a fourfold class: there is feeling belonging to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, and feeling not included in any sphere. ⤵ As a fivefold class: there is the faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of gladness, the faculty of sadness, and the faculty of equanimity. This is the aggregate of feeling as a fivefold class. ⤵ As a sixfold class: there is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of feeling as a sixfold class. ⤵ As a sevenfold class: there is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of contact with the mind element, and feeling born of contact with the mind-consciousness element. This is the aggregate of feeling as a sevenfold class. ⤵ As an eightfold class: there is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact – which may be pleasant or painful – feeling born of contact with the mind element, and feeling born of contact with the mind-consciousness element. This is the aggregate of feeling as an eightfold class. ⤵ As a ninefold class: there is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of contact with the mind element, and feeling born of contact with the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the aggregate of feeling as a ninefold class. ⤵ As a tenfold class: there is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact – which may be pleasant or painful – feeling born of contact with the mind element, and feeling born of contact with the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the aggregate of feeling as a tenfold class.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling with a root cause, and feeling without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is feeling that is a result, feeling that produces results, and feeling that is neither. There is feeling taken up at birth and able to be clung to, feeling not taken up but able to be clung to, and feeling neither taken up nor able to be clung to. There is feeling that is defiled and open to defilement, feeling undefiled yet open to defilement, and feeling neither defiled nor open to defilement. There is feeling with both thought and examination, feeling without thought but with examination only, and feeling with neither thought nor examination. There is feeling to be abandoned by seeing, feeling to be abandoned by meditative development, and feeling to be abandoned by neither. There is feeling whose root causes are to be abandoned by seeing, whose root causes are to be abandoned by development, and whose root causes are to be abandoned by neither. There is feeling leading to further accumulation, feeling leading to dismantling, and feeling leading to neither. There is feeling of trainees, feeling of those beyond training, and feeling of neither. There is limited feeling, expanded feeling, and measureless feeling. There is feeling with a limited object, feeling with an expanded object, and feeling with a measureless object. There is inferior feeling, middling feeling, and superior feeling. There is feeling fixed in wrongness, feeling fixed in rightness, and feeling not fixed. There is feeling with the path as its object, feeling with the path as its cause, and feeling with the path as its dominant factor. There is feeling that has arisen, feeling that has not arisen, and feeling bound to arise. There is past feeling, future feeling, and present feeling. There is feeling with a past object, feeling with a future object, and feeling with a present object. There is internal feeling, external feeling, and feeling both internal and external. There is feeling with an internal object, feeling with an external object, and feeling with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling joined with root causes, and feeling dissociated from them… there is feeling that is not itself a root cause but has one, and feeling that is not a root cause and has none. There is worldly feeling, and feeling beyond the world. There is feeling knowable by some kinds of consciousness, and feeling not knowable by some. There is feeling subject to the mental taints, and feeling free of them. There is feeling joined with the taints, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling dissociated from the taints yet still subject to them, and feeling dissociated from the taints and free of them. There is feeling that the fetters can bind, and feeling they cannot. There is feeling joined with the fetters, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling dissociated from the fetters yet still able to be bound, and feeling dissociated from them and unable to be bound. There is feeling that the ties can tie, and feeling they cannot. There is feeling joined with the ties, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling dissociated from the ties yet still able to be tied, and feeling dissociated from them and unable to be tied. There is feeling that the floods can sweep away, and feeling they cannot. There is feeling joined with the floods, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling dissociated from the floods yet still able to be swept away, and feeling dissociated from them and unable to be swept away. There is feeling that the yokes can bind, and feeling they cannot. There is feeling joined with the yokes, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling dissociated from the yokes yet still able to be yoked, and feeling dissociated from them and unable to be yoked. There is feeling that the hindrances can obstruct, and feeling they cannot. There is feeling joined with the hindrances, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling dissociated from the hindrances yet still able to be obstructed, and feeling dissociated from them and unable to be obstructed. There is feeling that can be wrongly grasped, and feeling that cannot. There is feeling joined with wrong grasping, and feeling dissociated from it. There is feeling dissociated from wrong grasping yet still able to be wrongly grasped, and feeling dissociated from it and unable to be wrongly grasped. There is feeling taken up at birth, and feeling not taken up. There is feeling that can be clung to, and feeling that cannot. There is feeling joined with clinging, and feeling dissociated from it. There is feeling dissociated from clinging yet still able to be clung to, and feeling dissociated from it and unable to be clung to. There is feeling open to defilement, and feeling not open to it. There is defiled feeling, and undefiled feeling. There is feeling joined with the defilements, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling dissociated from the defilements yet still open to defilement, and feeling dissociated from them and not open to defilement. There is feeling to be abandoned by seeing, and feeling not to be abandoned by seeing. There is feeling to be abandoned by meditative development, and feeling not to be abandoned by development. There is feeling whose root causes are to be abandoned by seeing, and feeling whose root causes are not. There is feeling whose root causes are to be abandoned by development, and feeling whose root causes are not. There is feeling with thought, and feeling without thought. There is feeling with examination, and feeling without examination. There is feeling with joy, and feeling without joy. There is feeling accompanied by joy, and feeling not accompanied by joy. There is feeling belonging to the sense sphere, and feeling not belonging to it. There is feeling belonging to the fine-material sphere, and feeling not belonging to it. There is feeling belonging to the immaterial sphere, and feeling not belonging to it. There is feeling included in the round of existence, and feeling outside it. There is feeling that leads out of the round, and feeling that does not. There is feeling fixed in its outcome, and feeling not fixed. There is feeling that can be surpassed, and feeling that cannot. There is feeling involving conflict, and feeling free from conflict. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, and neutral feeling… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling involving conflict, and feeling free from conflict. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is feeling that is a result, feeling that produces results, and feeling that is neither. There is feeling taken up at birth and able to be clung to… there is feeling with an internal object, feeling with an external object, and feeling with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.
The set rooted in the pairs.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling with a root cause, and feeling without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, and neutral feeling… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling joined with root causes, and feeling dissociated from them. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, and neutral feeling… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling that is not itself a root cause but has one, and feeling that is not a root cause and has none. There is worldly feeling, and feeling beyond the world. There is feeling knowable by some kinds of consciousness, and feeling not knowable by some. There is feeling subject to the mental taints, and feeling free of them. There is feeling joined with the taints, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling dissociated from the taints yet still subject to them, and feeling dissociated from the taints and free of them… there is feeling involving conflict, and feeling free from conflict. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, and neutral feeling… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.
2. Vedanākkhandho

Tattha katamo vedanākkhandho? Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. ⤵ Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato. ⤵ Catubbidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. ⤵ Pañcavidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sukhindriyaṃ, atthi dukkhindriyaṃ, atthi somanassindriyaṃ, atthi domanassindriyaṃ, atthi upekkhindriyaṃ. Evaṃ pañcavidhena vedanākkhandho. ⤵ Chabbidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ chabbidhena vedanākkhandho. ⤵ Sattavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ sattavidhena vedanākkhandho. ⤵ Aṭṭhavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā atthi sukhā, atthi dukkhā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena vedanākkhandho. ⤵ Navavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ navavidhena vedanākkhandho. ⤵ Dasavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā atthi sukhā, atthi dukkhā, manodhātusamphassajā vedanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā vedanā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

Atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho. Atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo. Atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo. Atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto. Atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati. Atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī. Atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno. Atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo. Atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.
