As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling with a root cause, and feeling without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is feeling that is a result, feeling that produces results, and feeling that is neither. There is feeling taken up at birth and able to be clung to, feeling not taken up but able to be clung to, and feeling neither taken up nor able to be clung to. There is feeling that is defiled and open to defilement, feeling undefiled yet open to defilement, and feeling neither defiled nor open to defilement. There is feeling with both thought and examination, feeling without thought but with examination only, and feeling with neither thought nor examination. There is feeling to be abandoned by seeing, feeling to be abandoned by meditative development, and feeling to be abandoned by neither. There is feeling whose root causes are to be abandoned by seeing, whose root causes are to be abandoned by development, and whose root causes are to be abandoned by neither. There is feeling leading to further accumulation, feeling leading to dismantling, and feeling leading to neither. There is feeling of trainees, feeling of those beyond training, and feeling of neither. There is limited feeling, expanded feeling, and measureless feeling. There is feeling with a limited object, feeling with an expanded object, and feeling with a measureless object. There is inferior feeling, middling feeling, and superior feeling. There is feeling fixed in wrongness, feeling fixed in rightness, and feeling not fixed. There is feeling with the path as its object, feeling with the path as its cause, and feeling with the path as its dominant factor. There is feeling that has arisen, feeling that has not arisen, and feeling bound to arise. There is past feeling, future feeling, and present feeling. There is feeling with a past object, feeling with a future object, and feeling with a present object. There is internal feeling, external feeling, and feeling both internal and external. There is feeling with an internal object, feeling with an external object, and feeling with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling joined with root causes, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling that is not itself a root cause but has one, and feeling that is not a root cause and has none. There is worldly feeling, and feeling beyond the world. There is feeling knowable by some kinds of consciousness, and feeling not knowable by some. There is feeling subject to the mental taints, and feeling free of them. There is feeling joined with the taints, and feeling dissociated from them. There is feeling dissociated from the taints yet still subject to them, and feeling dissociated from the taints and free of them. There is feeling that the fetters can bind, and feeling they cannot… there is feeling involving conflict, and feeling free from conflict. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is feeling with an internal object, feeling with an external object, and feeling with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.

Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo, atthi ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyo. ⤵ Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi oghaniyo, atthi anoghaniyo. ⤵ Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling joined with the floods, and feeling dissociated from them. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is past feeling, future feeling, and present feeling… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling dissociated from the floods yet still able to be swept away, and feeling dissociated from them and unable to be swept away. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is feeling with a past object, feeling with a future object, and feeling with a present object… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling that the yokes can bind, and feeling they cannot. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is internal feeling, external feeling, and feeling both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is feeling joined with the yokes, and feeling dissociated from them. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is feeling with an internal object, feeling with an external object, and feeling with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways.
The set expanding from both sides.

As a sevenfold class, the aggregate of feeling is this: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, neutral feeling, feeling belonging to the sense sphere, feeling belonging to the fine-material sphere, feeling belonging to the immaterial sphere, and feeling not included in any sphere. This is the aggregate of feeling as a sevenfold class.

As another sevenfold class: there is feeling that is a result… feeling with an internal object, feeling with an external object, feeling with an object both internal and external, feeling belonging to the sense sphere, feeling belonging to the fine-material sphere, feeling belonging to the immaterial sphere, and feeling not included in any sphere. This is the aggregate of feeling as a sevenfold class.

As a twenty-fourfold class, the aggregate of feeling is this: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral; and there is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of feeling as a twenty-fourfold class.

As another twenty-fourfold class: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may be a result… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external; and there is feeling born of eye-contact… feeling born of mind-contact. Through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may be a result… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external; and there is feeling born of eye-contact… feeling born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of feeling as a twenty-fourfold class.

As a thirtyfold class, the aggregate of feeling is this: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; and there is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of feeling as a thirtyfold class.

As a manifold class, the aggregate of feeling is this: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; and there is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of feeling as a manifold class.

As another manifold class: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may be a result… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of feeling may be a result… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; and there is feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of feeling as a manifold class.
This is called the aggregate of feeling.
3. The Aggregate of Perception

Therein, what is the aggregate of perception? As a single class, the aggregate of perception is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is perception with a root cause, and perception without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is wholesome perception, unwholesome perception, and neutral perception. ⤵ As a fourfold class: there is perception belonging to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, and perception not included in any sphere. ⤵ As a fivefold class: there is perception joined with the faculty of pleasure, joined with the faculty of pain, joined with the faculty of gladness, joined with the faculty of sadness, and joined with the faculty of equanimity. This is the aggregate of perception as a fivefold class. ⤵ As a sixfold class: there is perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of perception as a sixfold class. ⤵ As a sevenfold class: there is perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, perception born of contact with the mind element, and perception born of contact with the mind-consciousness element. This is the aggregate of perception as a sevenfold class. ⤵ As an eightfold class: there is perception born of eye-contact… perception born of body-contact – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – perception born of contact with the mind element, and perception born of contact with the mind-consciousness element. This is the aggregate of perception as an eightfold class. ⤵ As a ninefold class: there is perception born of eye-contact… perception born of body-contact, perception born of contact with the mind element, and perception born of contact with the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the aggregate of perception as a ninefold class. ⤵ As a tenfold class: there is perception born of eye-contact… perception born of body-contact – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – perception born of contact with the mind element, and perception born of contact with the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the aggregate of perception as a tenfold class.

As a single class, the aggregate of perception is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is perception with a root cause, and perception without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is perception joined with pleasant feeling, perception joined with painful feeling, and perception joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant… Thus the aggregate of perception is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of perception is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is perception with a root cause, and perception without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is perception that is a result, perception that produces results, and perception that is neither. There is perception taken up at birth and able to be clung to, perception not taken up but able to be clung to, and perception neither taken up nor able to be clung to. There is perception that is defiled and open to defilement, perception undefiled yet open to defilement, and perception neither defiled nor open to defilement. There is perception with both thought and examination, perception without thought but with examination only, and perception with neither thought nor examination. There is perception accompanied by joy, perception accompanied by happiness, and perception accompanied by equanimity. There is perception to be abandoned by seeing, perception to be abandoned by meditative development, and perception to be abandoned by neither. There is perception whose root causes are to be abandoned by seeing, whose root causes are to be abandoned by development, and whose root causes are to be abandoned by neither. There is perception leading to further accumulation, perception leading to dismantling, and perception leading to neither. There is perception of trainees, perception of those beyond training, and perception of neither. There is limited perception, expanded perception, and measureless perception. There is perception with a limited object, perception with an expanded object, and perception with a measureless object. There is inferior perception, middling perception, and superior perception. There is perception fixed in wrongness, perception fixed in rightness, and perception not fixed. There is perception with the path as its object, perception with the path as its cause, and perception with the path as its dominant factor. There is perception that has arisen, perception that has not arisen, and perception bound to arise. There is past perception, future perception, and present perception. There is perception with a past object, perception with a future object, and perception with a present object. There is internal perception, external perception, and perception both internal and external. There is perception with an internal object, perception with an external object, and perception with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of perception is classified up to ten ways.

Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi oghasampayutto, atthi oghavippayutto. ⤵ Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi oghavippayuttaoghaniyo, atthi oghavippayuttaanoghaniyo. ⤵ Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi yoganiyo, atthi ayoganiyo. ⤵ Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.

Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi yogasampayutto, atthi yogavippayutto. ⤵ Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho.
Ubhatovaḍḍhakaṃ.
Sattavidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena vedanākkhandho.

Aparopi sattavidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo , atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena vedanākkhandho.

Catuvīsatividhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; sotasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena vedanākkhandho.

Aparopi catuvīsatividhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, cakkhusamphassajā vedanā…pe… manosamphassajā vedanā; sotasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, cakkhusamphassajā vedanā…pe… manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena vedanākkhandho.

Tiṃsavidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ tiṃsavidhena vedanākkhandho.

Bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi kusalo , atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho.

Aparopi bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro , atthi apariyāpanno; sotasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho…pe… manosamphassapaccayā vedanākkhandho atthi vipāko…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo , atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro , atthi apariyāpanno; cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho.
Ayaṃ vuccati vedanākkhandho.
3. Saññākkhandho

Tattha katamo saññākkhandho? Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. ⤵ Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato. ⤵ Catubbidhena saññākkhandho – atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. ⤵ Pañcavidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sukhindriyasampayutto, atthi dukkhindriyasampayutto, atthi somanassindriyasampayutto, atthi domanassindriyasampayutto, atthi upekkhindriyasampayutto. Evaṃ pañcavidhena saññākkhandho. ⤵ Chabbidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā saññā, manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ chabbidhena saññākkhandho. ⤵ Sattavidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā saññā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ sattavidhena saññākkhandho. ⤵ Aṭṭhavidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… kāyasamphassajā saññā atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi dukkhasahagatā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena saññākkhandho. ⤵ Navavidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… kāyasamphassajā saññā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ navavidhena saññākkhandho. ⤵ Dasavidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… kāyasamphassajā saññā atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi dukkhasahagatā, manodhātusamphassajā saññā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā saññā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. ⤵ Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. ⤵ Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro. Atthi pītisahagato, atthi sukhasahagato, atthi upekkhāsahagato. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho. Atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo. Atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo. Atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto. Atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati. Atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī. Atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno. Atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo. Atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

As a single class, the aggregate of perception is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is perception joined with root causes, and perception dissociated from them. There is perception that is not itself a root cause but has one, and perception that is not a root cause and has none. There is worldly perception, and perception beyond the world. There is perception knowable by some kinds of consciousness, and perception not knowable by some. There is perception subject to the mental taints, and perception free of them. There is perception joined with the taints, and perception dissociated from them. There is perception dissociated from the taints yet still subject to them, and perception dissociated from the taints and free of them. There is perception that the fetters can bind, and perception they cannot. There is perception joined with the fetters, and perception dissociated from them. There is perception dissociated from the fetters yet still able to be bound, and perception dissociated from them and unable to be bound. There is perception that the ties can tie, and perception they cannot. There is perception joined with the ties, and perception dissociated from them. There is perception dissociated from the ties yet still able to be tied, and perception dissociated from them and unable to be tied. There is perception that the floods can sweep away, and perception they cannot. There is perception joined with the floods, and perception dissociated from them. There is perception dissociated from the floods yet still able to be swept away, and perception dissociated from them and unable to be swept away. There is perception that the yokes can bind, and perception they cannot. There is perception joined with the yokes, and perception dissociated from them. There is perception dissociated from the yokes yet still able to be yoked, and perception dissociated from them and unable to be yoked. There is perception that the hindrances can obstruct, and perception they cannot. There is perception joined with the hindrances, and perception dissociated from them. There is perception dissociated from the hindrances yet still able to be obstructed, and perception dissociated from them and unable to be obstructed. There is perception that can be wrongly grasped, and perception that cannot. There is perception joined with wrong grasping, and perception dissociated from it. There is perception dissociated from wrong grasping yet still able to be wrongly grasped, and perception dissociated from it and unable to be wrongly grasped. There is perception taken up at birth, and perception not taken up. There is perception that can be clung to, and perception that cannot. There is perception joined with clinging, and perception dissociated from it. There is perception dissociated from clinging yet still able to be clung to, and perception dissociated from it and unable to be clung to. There is perception open to defilement, and perception not open to it. There is defiled perception, and undefiled perception. There is perception joined with the defilements, and perception dissociated from them. There is perception dissociated from the defilements yet still open to defilement, and perception dissociated from them and not open to defilement. There is perception to be abandoned by seeing, and perception not to be abandoned by seeing. There is perception to be abandoned by meditative development, and perception not to be abandoned by development. There is perception whose root causes are to be abandoned by seeing, and perception whose root causes are not. There is perception whose root causes are to be abandoned by development, and perception whose root causes are not. There is perception with thought, and perception without thought. There is perception with examination, and perception without examination. There is perception with joy, and perception without joy. There is perception accompanied by joy, and perception not accompanied by joy. There is perception accompanied by happiness, and perception not accompanied by happiness. There is perception accompanied by equanimity, and perception not accompanied by equanimity. There is perception belonging to the sense sphere, and perception not belonging to it. There is perception belonging to the fine-material sphere, and perception not belonging to it. There is perception belonging to the immaterial sphere, and perception not belonging to it. There is perception included in the round of existence, and perception outside it. There is perception that leads out of the round, and perception that does not. There is perception fixed in its outcome, and perception not fixed. There is perception that can be surpassed, and perception that cannot. There is perception involving conflict, and perception free from conflict. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is wholesome perception, unwholesome perception, and neutral perception… Thus the aggregate of perception is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of perception is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is perception joined with the yokes, and perception dissociated from them. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is perception with a past object, perception with a future object, and perception with a present object… Thus the aggregate of perception is classified up to ten ways.

The set expanding from both sides.

As a sevenfold class, the aggregate of perception is this: there is wholesome perception, unwholesome perception, neutral perception, perception belonging to the sense sphere, perception belonging to the fine-material sphere, perception belonging to the immaterial sphere, and perception not included in any sphere. This is the aggregate of perception as a sevenfold class.

As another sevenfold class: there is perception joined with pleasant feeling, perception joined with painful feeling, perception joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, perception belonging to the sense sphere, perception belonging to the fine-material sphere, perception belonging to the immaterial sphere, and perception not included in any sphere… there is perception with an internal object, perception with an external object, perception with an object both internal and external, perception belonging to the sense sphere, perception belonging to the fine-material sphere, perception belonging to the immaterial sphere, and perception not included in any sphere. This is the aggregate of perception as a sevenfold class.

As a twenty-fourfold class, the aggregate of perception is this: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral; and there is perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of perception as a twenty-fourfold class.

As another twenty-fourfold class: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may be joined with pleasant feeling… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external; and there is perception born of eye-contact… perception born of mind-contact. Through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may be joined with pleasant feeling… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external; and there is perception born of eye-contact… perception born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of perception as a twenty-fourfold class.

As a thirtyfold class, the aggregate of perception is this: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; and there is perception born of eye-contact… perception born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of perception as a thirtyfold class.

As a manifold class, the aggregate of perception is this: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; and there is perception born of eye-contact… perception born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of perception as a manifold class.

As another manifold class: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may be joined with pleasant feeling… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of perception may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; and there is perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact, perception born of body-contact, and perception born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of perception as a manifold class.
This is called the aggregate of perception.

Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi yogavippayuttayoganiyo, atthi yogavippayuttaayoganiyo. ⤵ Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.

Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi nīvaraṇiyo, atthi anīvaraṇiyo. ⤵ Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho.
Ubhatovaḍḍhakaṃ.
Sattavidhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena saññākkhandho.

Aparopi sattavidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. Evaṃ sattavidhena saññākkhandho.

Catuvīsatividhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato; cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā saññā, manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena saññākkhandho.

Aparopi catuvīsatividhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… manosamphassajā saññā. Sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo; cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ catuvīsatividhena saññākkhandho.

Tiṃsatividhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā …pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ tiṃsatividhena saññākkhandho.

Bahuvidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, sotasamphassapaccayā …pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato, atthi kāmāvacaro , atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, cakkhusamphassajā saññā…pe… manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena saññākkhandho.

Aparopi bahuvidhena saññākkhandho – cakkhusamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, sotasamphassapaccayā…pe… ghānasamphassapaccayā…pe… jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… kāyasamphassapaccayā…pe… manosamphassapaccayā saññākkhandho atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo, atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno, cakkhusamphassajā saññā, sotasamphassajā saññā, ghānasamphassajā saññā, jivhāsamphassajā saññā, kāyasamphassajā saññā, manosamphassajā saññā. Evaṃ bahuvidhena saññākkhandho.
Ayaṃ vuccati saññākkhandho.
4. The Aggregate of Mental Formations

Therein, what is the aggregate of mental formations? As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes, and formations that are not. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, and neutral formations. ⤵ As a fourfold class: there are formations belonging to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, and formations not included in any sphere. ⤵ As a fivefold class: there are formations joined with the faculty of pleasure, joined with the faculty of pain, joined with the faculty of gladness, joined with the faculty of sadness, and joined with the faculty of equanimity. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a fivefold class. ⤵ As a sixfold class: there is intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, and intention born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a sixfold class. ⤵ As a sevenfold class: there is intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, intention born of contact with the mind element, and intention born of contact with the mind-consciousness element. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a sevenfold class. ⤵ As an eightfold class: there is intention born of eye-contact… intention born of body-contact – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – intention born of contact with the mind element, and intention born of contact with the mind-consciousness element. This is the aggregate of mental formations as an eightfold class. ⤵ As a ninefold class: there is intention born of eye-contact… intention born of contact with the mind element, and intention born of contact with the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a ninefold class. ⤵ As a tenfold class: there is intention born of eye-contact… intention born of body-contact – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – intention born of contact with the mind element, and intention born of contact with the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a tenfold class.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes, and formations that are not. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations joined with pleasant feeling, formations joined with painful feeling, and formations joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. There are formations that are results, formations that produce results, and formations that are neither. There are formations taken up at birth and able to be clung to, formations not taken up but able to be clung to, and formations neither taken up nor able to be clung to. There are formations that are defiled and open to defilement, formations undefiled yet open to defilement, and formations neither defiled nor open to defilement. There are formations with both thought and examination, formations without thought but with examination only, and formations with neither thought nor examination. There are formations accompanied by joy, formations accompanied by happiness, and formations accompanied by equanimity. There are formations to be abandoned by seeing, formations to be abandoned by meditative development, and formations to be abandoned by neither. There are formations whose root causes are to be abandoned by seeing, whose root causes are to be abandoned by development, and whose root causes are to be abandoned by neither. There are formations leading to further accumulation, formations leading to dismantling, and formations leading to neither. There are formations of trainees, formations of those beyond training, and formations of neither. There are limited formations, expanded formations, and measureless formations. There are formations with a limited object, formations with an expanded object, and formations with a measureless object. There are inferior formations, middling formations, and superior formations. There are formations fixed in wrongness, formations fixed in rightness, and formations not fixed. There are formations with the path as their object, formations with the path as their cause, and formations with the path as their dominant factor. There are formations that have arisen, formations that have not arisen, and formations bound to arise. There are past formations, future formations, and present formations. There are formations with a past object, formations with a future object, and formations with a present object. There are internal formations, external formations, and formations both internal and external. There are formations with an internal object, formations with an external object, and formations with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations with a root cause, and formations without one. There are formations joined with root causes, and formations dissociated from them. There are formations that are root causes and have root causes, and formations that have root causes but are not themselves root causes. There are formations that are root causes and are joined with root causes, and formations joined with root causes that are not themselves root causes. There are formations that are not root causes but have them, and formations that are not root causes and have none. There are worldly formations, and formations beyond the world. There are formations knowable by some kinds of consciousness, and formations not knowable by some. There are formations that are mental taints, and formations that are not. There are formations subject to the taints, and formations free of them. There are formations joined with the taints, and formations dissociated from them. There are formations that are taints and are subject to them, and formations subject to the taints that are not themselves taints. There are formations that are taints and are joined with them, and formations joined with the taints that are not themselves taints. There are formations dissociated from the taints yet still subject to them, and formations dissociated from the taints and free of them. There are formations that are fetters, and formations that are not. There are formations that the fetters can bind, and formations they cannot. There are formations joined with the fetters, and formations dissociated from them. There are formations that are fetters and can be bound, and formations that can be bound but are not themselves fetters. There are formations that are fetters and are joined with them, and formations joined with the fetters that are not themselves fetters. There are formations dissociated from the fetters yet still able to be bound, and formations dissociated from them and unable to be bound. ⤵ There are formations that are ties, and formations that are not. There are formations that the ties can tie, and formations they cannot. There are formations joined with the ties, and formations dissociated from them. There are formations that are ties and can be tied, and formations that can be tied but are not themselves ties. There are formations that are ties and are joined with them, and formations joined with the ties that are not themselves ties. There are formations dissociated from the ties yet still able to be tied, and formations dissociated from them and unable to be tied. There are formations that are floods, and formations that are not. There are formations that the floods can sweep away, and formations they cannot. There are formations joined with the floods, and formations dissociated from them. There are formations that are floods and can be swept away, and formations that can be swept away but are not themselves floods. There are formations that are floods and are joined with them, and formations joined with the floods that are not themselves floods. There are formations dissociated from the floods yet still able to be swept away, and formations dissociated from them and unable to be swept away. There are formations that are yokes, and formations that are not. There are formations that the yokes can bind, and formations they cannot. There are formations joined with the yokes, and formations dissociated from them. There are formations that are yokes and can be yoked, and formations that can be yoked but are not themselves yokes. There are formations that are yokes and are joined with them, and formations joined with the yokes that are not themselves yokes. There are formations dissociated from the yokes yet still able to be yoked, and formations dissociated from them and unable to be yoked. There are formations that are hindrances, and formations that are not. There are formations that the hindrances can obstruct, and formations they cannot. There are formations joined with the hindrances, and formations dissociated from them. There are formations that are hindrances and can be obstructed, and formations that can be obstructed but are not themselves hindrances. There are formations that are hindrances and are joined with them, and formations joined with the hindrances that are not themselves hindrances. There are formations dissociated from the hindrances yet still able to be obstructed, and formations dissociated from them and unable to be obstructed. ⤵ There are formations that are wrong grasping, and formations that are not. There are formations that can be wrongly grasped, and formations that cannot. There are formations joined with wrong grasping, and formations dissociated from it. There are formations that are wrong grasping and can be wrongly grasped, and formations that can be wrongly grasped but are not themselves wrong grasping. There are formations dissociated from wrong grasping yet still able to be wrongly grasped, and formations dissociated from it and unable to be wrongly grasped. There are formations taken up at birth, and formations not taken up. There are formations that are clinging, and formations that are not. There are formations that can be clung to, and formations that cannot. There are formations joined with clinging, and formations dissociated from it. There are formations that are clinging and can be clung to, and formations that can be clung to but are not themselves clinging. There are formations that are clinging and are joined with it, and formations joined with clinging that are not themselves clinging. There are formations dissociated from clinging yet still able to be clung to, and formations dissociated from it and unable to be clung to. ⤵ There are formations that are defilements, and formations that are not. There are formations open to defilement, and formations not open to it. There are defiled formations, and undefiled formations. There are formations joined with the defilements, and formations dissociated from them. There are formations that are defilements and are open to defilement, and formations open to defilement that are not themselves defilements. There are formations that are defilements and are defiled, and formations that are defiled but are not themselves defilements. There are formations that are defilements and are joined with them, and formations joined with the defilements that are not themselves defilements. There are formations dissociated from the defilements yet still open to defilement, and formations dissociated from them and not open to defilement. There are formations to be abandoned by seeing, and formations not to be abandoned by seeing. There are formations to be abandoned by meditative development, and formations not to be abandoned by development. There are formations whose root causes are to be abandoned by seeing, and formations whose root causes are not. There are formations whose root causes are to be abandoned by development, and formations whose root causes are not. ⤵ There are formations with thought, and formations without thought. There are formations with examination, and formations without examination. There are formations with joy, and formations without joy. There are formations accompanied by joy, and formations not accompanied by joy. There are formations accompanied by happiness, and formations not accompanied by happiness. There are formations accompanied by equanimity, and formations not accompanied by equanimity. There are formations belonging to the sense sphere, and formations not belonging to it. There are formations belonging to the fine-material sphere, and formations not belonging to it. There are formations belonging to the immaterial sphere, and formations not belonging to it. There are formations included in the round of existence, and formations outside it. There are formations that lead out of the round, and formations that do not. There are formations fixed in their outcome, and formations not fixed. There are formations that can be surpassed, and formations that cannot. There are formations involving conflict, and formations free from conflict. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, and neutral formations… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations involving conflict, and formations free from conflict. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations joined with pleasant feeling… there are formations with an internal object, formations with an external object, and formations with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.
The set rooted in the pairs.
4. Saṅkhārakkhandho

Tattha katamo saṅkhārakkhandho? Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu, atthi na hetu. ⤵ Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kusalo , atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato. ⤵ Catubbidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi apariyāpanno. ⤵ Pañcavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sukhindriyasampayutto, atthi dukkhindriyasampayutto, atthi somanassindriyasampayutto, atthi domanassindriyasampayutto, atthi upekkhindriyasampayutto. Evaṃ pañcavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho. ⤵ Chabbidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā, sotasamphassajā cetanā, ghānasamphassajā cetanā, jivhāsamphassajā cetanā, kāyasamphassajā cetanā, manosamphassajā cetanā. Evaṃ chabbidhena saṅkhārakkhandho. ⤵ Sattavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā, sotasamphassajā cetanā, ghānasamphassajā cetanā, jivhāsamphassajā cetanā, kāyasamphassajā cetanā, manodhātusamphassajā cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā. Evaṃ sattavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho. ⤵ Aṭṭhavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… kāyasamphassajā cetanā atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi dukkhasahagatā, manodhātusamphassajā cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā . Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho. ⤵ Navavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… manodhātusamphassajā cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ navavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho. ⤵ Dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… kāyasamphassajā cetanā atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi dukkhasahagatā, manodhātusamphassajā cetanā, manoviññāṇadhātusamphassajā cetanā atthi kusalā, atthi akusalā, atthi abyākatā. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu, atthi na hetu. ⤵ Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto, atthi adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto. Atthi vipāko, atthi vipākadhammadhammo, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo. Atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro. Atthi pītisahagato, atthi sukhasahagato, atthi upekkhāsahagato. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. Atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī. Atthi sekkho, atthi asekkho, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkho. Atthi paritto, atthi mahaggato, atthi appamāṇo. Atthi parittārammaṇo, atthi mahaggatārammaṇo, atthi appamāṇārammaṇo. Atthi hīno, atthi majjhimo, atthi paṇīto. Atthi micchattaniyato, atthi sammattaniyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi maggārammaṇo, atthi maggahetuko, atthi maggādhipati. Atthi uppanno, atthi anuppanno, atthi uppādī. Atthi atīto, atthi anāgato, atthi paccuppanno. Atthi atītārammaṇo, atthi anāgatārammaṇo, atthi paccuppannārammaṇo. Atthi ajjhatto, atthi bahiddho, atthi ajjhattabahiddho . Atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Atthi hetusampayutto, atthi hetuvippayutto. Atthi hetu ceva sahetuko ca, atthi sahetuko ceva na ca hetu. Atthi hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, atthi hetusampayutto ceva na ca hetu. Atthi na hetu sahetuko, atthi na hetu ahetuko. Atthi lokiyo, atthi lokuttaro. Atthi kenaci viññeyyo, atthi kenaci na viññeyyo. Atthi āsavo, atthi no āsavo. Atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo. Atthi āsavasampayutto, atthi āsavavippayutto. Atthi āsavo ceva sāsavo ca, atthi sāsavo ceva no ca āsavo. Atthi āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca, atthi āsavasampayutto ceva no ca āsavo. Atthi āsavavippayuttasāsavo, atthi āsavavippayuttaanāsavo. Atthi saṃyojanaṃ, atthi no saṃyojanaṃ. Atthi saṃyojaniyo, atthi asaṃyojaniyo. Atthi saṃyojanasampayutto, atthi saṃyojanavippayutto. Atthi saṃyojanañceva saṃyojaniyo ca, atthi saṃyojaniyo ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ. Atthi saṃyojanañceva saṃyojanasampayutto ca, atthi saṃyojanasampayutto ceva no ca saṃyojanaṃ. Atthi saṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyo, atthi saṃyojanavippayuttaasaṃyojaniyo. ⤵ Atthi gantho, atthi no gantho. Atthi ganthaniyo, atthi aganthaniyo. Atthi ganthasampayutto, atthi ganthavippayutto. Atthi gantho ceva ganthaniyo ca, atthi ganthaniyo ceva no ca gantho. Atthi gantho ceva ganthasampayutto ca, atthi ganthasampayutto ceva no ca gantho. Atthi ganthavippayuttaganthaniyo, atthi ganthavippayuttaaganthaniyo. Atthi ogho, atthi no ogho. Atthi oghaniyo, atthi anoghaniyo. Atthi oghasampayutto, atthi oghavippayutto. Atthi ogho ceva oghaniyo ca, atthi oghaniyo ceva no ca ogho. Atthi ogho ceva oghasampayutto ca, atthi oghasampayutto ceva no ca ogho. Atthi oghavippayuttaoghaniyo, atthi oghavippayuttaanoghaniyo. Atthi yogo, atthi no yogo. Atthi yoganiyo, atthi ayoganiyo. Atthi yogasampayutto, atthi yogavippayutto. Atthi yogo ceva yoganiyo ca, atthi yoganiyo ceva no ca yogo. Atthi yogo ceva yogasampayutto ca, atthi yogasampayutto ceva no ca yogo. Atthi yogavippayuttayoganiyo, atthi yogavippayuttaayoganiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇaṃ, atthi no nīvaraṇaṃ. Atthi nīvaraṇiyo, atthi anīvaraṇiyo. Atthi nīvaraṇasampayutto, atthi nīvaraṇavippayutto. Atthi nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇiyo ca, atthi nīvaraṇiyo ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ. Atthi nīvaraṇañceva nīvaraṇasampayutto ca, atthi nīvaraṇasampayutto ceva no ca nīvaraṇaṃ. Atthi nīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyo, atthi nīvaraṇavippayuttaanīvaraṇiyo. ⤵ Atthi parāmāso, atthi no parāmāso. Atthi parāmaṭṭho, atthi aparāmaṭṭho. Atthi parāmāsasampayutto, atthi parāmāsavippayutto. Atthi parāmāso ceva parāmaṭṭho ca, atthi parāmaṭṭho ceva no ca parāmāso. Atthi parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭho, atthi parāmāsavippayuttaaparāmaṭṭho. Atthi upādinno, atthi anupādinno. Atthi upādānaṃ, atthi no upādānaṃ. Atthi upādāniyo, atthi anupādāniyo. Atthi upādānasampayutto, atthi upādānavippayutto. Atthi upādānañceva upādāniyo ca, atthi upādāniyo ceva no ca upādānaṃ. Atthi upādānañceva upādānasampayutto ca , atthi upādānasampayutto ceva no ca upādānaṃ. Atthi upādānavippayuttaupādāniyo, atthi upādānavippayuttaanupādāniyo. ⤵ Atthi kileso, atthi no kileso. Atthi saṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkilesiko. Atthi saṃkiliṭṭho, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭho. Atthi kilesasampayutto, atthi kilesavippayutto. Atthi kileso ceva saṃkilesiko ca, atthi saṃkilesiko ceva no ca kileso. Atthi kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca, atthi saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso. Atthi kileso ceva kilesasampayutto ca, atthi kilesasampayutto ceva no ca kileso. Atthi kilesavippayuttasaṃkilesiko, atthi kilesavippayuttaasaṃkilesiko. Atthi dassanena pahātabbo, atthi na dassanena pahātabbo. Atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbo, atthi na bhāvanāya pahātabbo. Atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi na dassanena pahātabbahetuko. Atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko. ⤵ Atthi savitakko, atthi avitakko. Atthi savicāro, atthi avicāro. Atthi sappītiko , atthi appītiko. Atthi pītisahagato, atthi na pītisahagato. Atthi sukhasahagato, atthi na sukhasahagato. Atthi upekkhāsahagato, atthi na upekkhāsahagato. Atthi kāmāvacaro, atthi na kāmāvacaro. Atthi rūpāvacaro, atthi na rūpāvacaro. Atthi arūpāvacaro, atthi na arūpāvacaro. Atthi pariyāpanno, atthi apariyāpanno. Atthi niyyāniko, atthi aniyyāniko. Atthi niyato, atthi aniyato. Atthi sauttaro, atthi anuttaro. Atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo. ⤵ Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi saraṇo, atthi araṇo. ⤵ Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto…pe… atthi ajjhattārammaṇo, atthi bahiddhārammaṇo, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.
Dukamūlakaṃ.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes, and formations that are not. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, and neutral formations… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations involving conflict, and formations free from conflict. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, and neutral formations… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes, and formations that are not. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations with an internal object, formations with an external object, and formations with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations involving conflict, and formations free from conflict. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations with an internal object, formations with an external object, and formations with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.
The set rooted in the triads.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes, and formations that are not. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, and neutral formations… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class, the aggregate of mental formations: there are formations with a root cause, and formations without one. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations joined with pleasant feeling, formations joined with painful feeling, and formations joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations joined with root causes, and formations dissociated from them. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations that are results, formations that produce results, and formations that are neither… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes and have root causes, and formations that have root causes but are not themselves root causes. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations taken up at birth and able to be clung to, formations not taken up but able to be clung to, and formations neither taken up nor able to be clung to… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes and are joined with root causes, and formations joined with root causes that are not themselves root causes. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations that are defiled and open to defilement, formations undefiled yet open to defilement, and formations neither defiled nor open to defilement… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are not root causes but have them, and formations that are not root causes and have none. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations with both thought and examination, formations without thought but with examination only, and formations with neither thought nor examination… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are worldly formations, and formations beyond the world. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations accompanied by joy, formations accompanied by happiness, and formations accompanied by equanimity… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations knowable by some kinds of consciousness, and formations not knowable by some. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations to be abandoned by seeing, formations to be abandoned by meditative development, and formations to be abandoned by neither… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are mental taints, and formations that are not. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations whose root causes are to be abandoned by seeing, whose root causes are to be abandoned by development, and whose root causes are to be abandoned by neither… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations subject to the taints, and formations free of them. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations leading to further accumulation, formations leading to dismantling, and formations leading to neither… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu ceva sahetuko ca, atthi sahetuko ceva na ca hetu. ⤵ Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi upādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnupādāniyo, atthi anupādinnaanupādāniyo…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca, atthi hetusampayutto ceva na ca hetu. ⤵ Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesiko, atthi asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesiko…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi na hetu sahetuko, atthi na hetu ahetuko. ⤵ Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi savitakkasavicāro, atthi avitakkavicāramatto, atthi avitakkaavicāro…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi āsavo, atthi no āsavo. ⤵ Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi dassanena pahātabbahetuko, atthi bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko, atthi neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. ⤵ Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi sāsavo, atthi anāsavo. ⤵ Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi ācayagāmī, atthi apacayagāmī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī…pe…. Evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations joined with the taints, and formations dissociated from them. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations of trainees, formations of those beyond training, and formations of neither… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are taints and are subject to them, and formations subject to the taints that are not themselves taints. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are limited formations, expanded formations, and measureless formations… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are taints and are joined with them, and formations joined with the taints that are not themselves taints. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations with a limited object, formations with an expanded object, and formations with a measureless object… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations dissociated from the taints yet still subject to them, and formations dissociated from the taints and free of them. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are inferior formations, middling formations, and superior formations… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are fetters, and formations that are not. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations fixed in wrongness, formations fixed in rightness, and formations not fixed… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that the fetters can bind, and formations they cannot. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations with the path as their object, formations with the path as their cause, and formations with the path as their dominant factor… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations joined with the fetters, and formations dissociated from them. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations that have arisen, formations that have not arisen, and formations bound to arise… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are fetters and can be bound, and formations that can be bound but are not themselves fetters. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are past formations, future formations, and present formations… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are fetters and are joined with them, and formations joined with the fetters that are not themselves fetters. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations with a past object, formations with a future object, and formations with a present object… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations dissociated from the fetters yet still able to be bound, and formations dissociated from them and unable to be bound. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are internal formations, external formations, and formations both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.

As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: it is joined with mind. ⤵ As a twofold class: there are formations that are ties, and formations that are not. ⤵ As a threefold class: there are formations with an internal object, formations with an external object, and formations with an object both internal and external… Thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways.
The set expanding from both sides.

As a sevenfold class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, neutral formations; formations belonging to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, and formations not included in any sphere. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a sevenfold class.

As another sevenfold class: there are formations joined with pleasant feeling, formations joined with painful feeling, formations joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant; formations belonging to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, and formations not included in any sphere… there are formations with an internal object, formations with an external object, formations with an object both internal and external; formations belonging to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, and formations not included in any sphere. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a sevenfold class.

As a twenty-fourfold class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral; and there is intention born of eye-contact… intention born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a twenty-fourfold class.

As another twenty-fourfold class: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may be joined with pleasant feeling… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external; and there is intention born of eye-contact… intention born of mind-contact; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may be joined with pleasant feeling… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external; and there is intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, and intention born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a twenty-fourfold class.

As a thirtyfold class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; and there is intention born of eye-contact… intention born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a thirtyfold class.

As a manifold class, the aggregate of mental formations is this: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; and there is intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, and intention born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a manifold class.

As another manifold class: through eye-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; through ear-contact as its condition… through nose-contact as its condition… through tongue-contact as its condition… through body-contact as its condition… through mind-contact as its condition, the aggregate of formations may be joined with pleasant feeling… may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, may belong to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, or be not included in any sphere; and there is intention born of eye-contact, intention born of ear-contact, intention born of nose-contact, intention born of tongue-contact, intention born of body-contact, and intention born of mind-contact. This is the aggregate of mental formations as a manifold class.
This is called the aggregate of mental formations.
