3. Analysis of the Elements
1. Classification According to the Discourses
There are six elements – the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the air element, the space element, and the consciousness element.

Therein, what is the earth element? The earth element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal earth element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, internal and taken up at birth – namely: head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, and excrement; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal earth element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external earth element? Whatever externally is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, external and not taken up – namely: iron, copper, tin, lead, silver ore, pearl, gems, cat's-eye, conch shell, stone, coral, silver, gold, ruby, emerald, grass, wood, gravel, potsherds, earth, rock, and mountains; or whatever else externally is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external earth element'. The internal earth element and the external earth element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the earth element".

Therein, what is the water element? The water element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal water element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, internal and taken up at birth – namely: bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, mucus, joint fluid, and urine; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal water element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external water element? Whatever externally is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, external and not taken up – namely: the juice of roots, the juice of stems, the juice of bark, the juice of leaves, the juice of flowers, the juice of fruits, milk, curds, ghee, butter, oil, honey, molasses, and the waters of the earth or of the sky; or whatever else externally is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external water element'. The internal water element and the external water element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the water element".

Therein, what is the fire element? The fire element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal fire element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, internal and taken up at birth – namely: that by which one is warmed, that by which one ages, that by which one is burned, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is fully digested; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal fire element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external fire element? Whatever externally is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, external and not taken up – namely: fire of wood, fire of straw, fire of grass, fire of cow dung, fire of husks, fire of rubbish, lightning fire, the heat of fire, the heat of the sun, the heat of a heap of wood, the heat of a heap of grass, the heat of a heap of grain, the heat of a heap of goods; or whatever else externally is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external fire element'. The internal fire element and the external fire element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the fire element".

Therein, what is the air element? The air element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal air element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is air, airy, the distension of material form, internal and taken up at birth – namely: winds going upward, winds going downward, winds in the belly, winds in the bowels, winds coursing through the limbs, cutting winds, piercing winds, throbbing winds, breathing in and breathing out; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is air, airy, the distension of material form, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal air element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external air element? Whatever externally is air, airy, the distension of material form, external and not taken up – namely: east winds, west winds, north winds, south winds, dusty winds, dust-free winds, cold winds, hot winds, gentle winds, strong winds, black winds, high-altitude winds, winds from birds' wings, winds from a supaṇṇa bird, winds from palm-leaf fans, winds from a winnowing fan; or whatever else externally is air, airy, the distension of material form, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external air element'. The internal air element and the external air element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the air element".

Therein, what is the space element? The space element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal space element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is space, spatial, a void, a hollow, an opening, a gap, not touched by flesh and blood, internal and taken up at birth – namely: the opening of the ear, the opening of the nose, the door of the mouth, that by which one swallows what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted, that in which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted stays, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted passes out below; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is space, spatial, a void, a hollow, an opening, a gap, not touched by flesh and blood, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal space element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external space element? Whatever externally is space, spatial, a void, a hollow, an opening, a gap, not touched by the four great elements, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external space element'. The internal space element and the external space element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the space element".

Therein, what is the consciousness element? The eye-consciousness element, the ear-consciousness element, the nose-consciousness element, the tongue-consciousness element, the body-consciousness element, and the mind-consciousness element – this is called "the consciousness element".
These are the six elements.
There are another six elements – the pleasure element, the pain element, the gladness element, the sadness element, the equanimity element, and the ignorance element.

Therein, what is the pleasure element? Bodily comfort, bodily pleasure; the comfortable, pleasant experience born of body-contact; the comfortable, pleasant feeling born of body-contact – this is called "the pleasure element". ⤵ Therein, what is the pain element? Bodily discomfort, bodily pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of body-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of body-contact – this is called "the pain element". ⤵ Therein, what is the gladness element? Mental comfort, mental pleasure; the comfortable, pleasant experience born of mind-contact; the comfortable, pleasant feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "the gladness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the sadness element? Mental discomfort, mental pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of mind-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "the sadness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the equanimity element? What is mentally neither comfortable nor uncomfortable; the experience born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant; the feeling born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant – this is called "the equanimity element". ⤵ Therein, what is the ignorance element? Not knowing, not seeing, not comprehending, not awakening, not fully awakening, not penetrating, not grasping, not fathoming, not weighing evenly, not reflecting, not seeing directly; poor discernment, foolishness, lack of clear understanding; delusion, bewilderment, complete confusion; ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the barrier of ignorance; delusion, the root of the unwholesome – this is called "the ignorance element".
These are the six elements.
There are another six elements – the element of sense desire, the element of ill will, the element of cruelty, the element of renunciation, the element of goodwill, and the element of harmlessness.
3. Dhātuvibhaṅgo
1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ
Cha dhātuyo – pathavīdhātu [paṭhavīdhātu (sī. syā.) evamuparipi], āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu, ākāsadhātu, viññāṇadhātu.

Tattha katamā pathavīdhātu? Pathavīdhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru [nahāru (sī.)] aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ [aṭṭhimiñjā (sī.)] vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā pathavīdhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – ayo lohaṃ tipu sīsaṃ sajjhaṃ [sajjhu (syā.)] muttā maṇi veḷuriyo saṅkho silā pavāḷaṃ rajataṃ jātarūpaṃ lohitaṅko [lohitaṅgo (syā. ka.), lohitako (?)] masāragallaṃ tiṇaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sakkharā kaṭhalaṃ [kathalaṃ (ka.)] bhūmi pāsāṇo pabbato, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ kakkhaḷattaṃ kakkhaḷabhāvo bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā pathavīdhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu yā ca bāhirā pathavīdhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "pathavīdhātu".

Tattha katamā āpodhātu? Āpodhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā āpodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ [sneho snehagataṃ (syā.)] bandhanattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ bandhanattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā āpodhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā āpodhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ bandhanattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – mūlaraso khandharaso tacaraso pattaraso puppharaso phalaraso khīraṃ dadhi sappi navanītaṃ telaṃ madhu phāṇitaṃ bhummāni vā udakāni antalikkhāni vā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ āpo āpogataṃ sineho sinehagataṃ bandhanattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā āpodhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā āpodhātu yā ca bāhirā āpodhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "āpodhātu".

Tattha katamā tejodhātu? Tejodhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā tejodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – yena ca santappati yena ca jīrīyati yena ca pariḍayhati yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā tejodhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā tejodhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kaṭṭhaggi palālaggi [sakalikaggi (sabbattha)] tiṇaggi gomayaggi thusaggi saṅkāraggi indaggi aggisantāpo sūriyasantāpo kaṭṭhasannicayasantāpo tiṇasannicayasantāpo dhaññasannicayasantāpo bhaṇḍasannicayasantāpo, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ tejo tejogataṃ usmā usmāgataṃ usumaṃ usumagataṃ bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā tejodhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā tejodhātu yā ca bāhirā tejodhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "tejodhātu".

Tattha katamā vāyodhātu? Vāyodhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – uddhaṅgamā vātā adhogamā vātā kucchisayā vātā koṭṭhāsayā [koṭṭhasayā (sī. syā.)] vātā aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā satthakavātā khurakavātā uppalakavātā assāso passāso iti vā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā vāyodhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – puratthimā vātā pacchimā vātā uttarā vātā dakkhiṇā vātā sarajā vātā arajā vātā sītā vātā uṇhā vātā parittā vātā adhimattā vātā kāḷavātā verambhavātā pakkhavātā supaṇṇavātā tālavaṇṭavātā vidhūpanavātā, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi bāhiraṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ thambhitattaṃ rūpassa bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā vāyodhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā vāyodhātu yā ca bāhirā vāyodhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "vāyodhātu".

Tattha katamā ākāsadhātu? Ākāsadhātudvayaṃ – atthi ajjhattikā, atthi bāhirā. Tattha katamā ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ maṃsalohitehi ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kaṇṇacchiddaṃ nāsacchiddaṃ mukhadvāraṃ, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ ajjhoharati, yattha ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ santiṭṭhati, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ adhobhāgaṃ nikkhamati, yaṃ vā panaññampi atthi ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ maṃsalohitehi ajjhattaṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu’. ⤵ Tattha katamā bāhirā ākāsadhātu? Yaṃ bāhiraṃ ākāso ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaro vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ catūhi mahābhūtehi bahiddhā anupādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati ‘bāhirā ākāsadhātu’. Yā ca ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu yā ca bāhirā ākāsadhātu, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati "ākāsadhātu".
Tattha katamā viññāṇadhātu? Cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati "viññāṇadhātu".
Imā cha dhātuyo.
Aparāpi cha dhātuyo – sukhadhātu, dukkhadhātu, somanassadhātu, domanassadhātu, upekkhādhātu, avijjādhātu.

Tattha katamā sukhadhātu? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ sātaṃ kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "sukhadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā dukkhadhātu? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "dukkhadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā somanassadhātu? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ sātaṃ cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ sātaṃ sukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā sātā sukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "somanassadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā domanassadhātu? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "domanassadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā upekkhādhātu? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā adukkhamasukhā vedanā – ayaṃ vuccati "upekkhādhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā avijjādhātu? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ anabhisamayo ananubodho asambodho appaṭivedho asaṅgāhaṇā apariyogāhaṇā asamapekkhanā apaccavekkhaṇā apaccakkhakammaṃ dummejjhaṃ bālyaṃ asampajaññaṃ moho pamoho sammoho avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūlaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "avijjādhātu".
Imā cha dhātuyo.
Aparāpi cha dhātuyo – kāmadhātu, byāpādadhātu, vihiṃsādhātu, nekkhammadhātu, abyāpādadhātu, avihiṃsādhātu.

Therein, what is the element of sense desire? Thinking connected with sense desire – thought, intention, fixing, focusing, directing the mind, wrong intention – this is called the element of sense desire. Taking the Avīci hell as the lower limit and the gods who wield power over others' creations as the upper limit, whatever within this range moves here and is included here – the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields, material form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness – this is called "the element of sense desire". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of ill will? Thinking connected with ill will – thought… wrong intention – this is called "the element of ill will". Or the mind's irritation over the ten grounds for resentment: hostility, resistance, opposition; anger, rage, fury; hatred, ill feeling, malice; the mind's vexation, mental resentment; anger, being angry, the state of being angry; hatred, hating, the state of hating; vexation, being vexed; opposition, hostility; ferocity, harshness, and the mind's displeasure – this is called "the element of ill will". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of cruelty? Thinking connected with cruelty – thought… wrong intention – this is called "the element of cruelty". Here someone harms living beings with a hand, a clod, a stick, a knife, a rope, or with one thing or another; such tormenting, harassing, hurting, injuring, provoking, and attacking of others – this is called "the element of cruelty". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of renunciation? Thinking connected with renunciation – thought… right intention – this is called "the element of renunciation". Indeed, all wholesome states are "the element of renunciation". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of goodwill? Thinking connected with goodwill – thought… right intention – this is called "the element of goodwill". Loving-kindness towards living beings, the act of loving, the state of loving, the liberation of mind through loving-kindness – this is called "the element of goodwill". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of harmlessness? Thinking connected with harmlessness – thought, intention, fixing, focusing, directing the mind, right intention – this is called "the element of harmlessness". Compassion towards living beings, the act of compassion, the state of compassion, the liberation of mind through compassion – this is called "the element of harmlessness".
These are the six elements.
Thus these three sets of six, gathered and grouped together, make eighteen elements.
The Classification According to the Discourses is finished.
2. Classification According to the Abhidhamma

There are eighteen elements – the eye element, the element of sights, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the element of sounds, the ear-consciousness element; the nose element, the element of smells, the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the element of tastes, the tongue-consciousness element; the body element, the element of things touched, the body-consciousness element; the mind element, the element of mental objects, and the mind-consciousness element.

Therein, what is the eye element? The eye that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the eye element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of sights? The sight that is the shining of colour derived from the four great elements… this is the element of sights – this is called "the element of sights". ⤵ Therein, what is the eye-consciousness element? Depending on the eye and sights there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding eye-consciousness element – this is called "the eye-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the ear element? The ear that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the ear element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of sounds? The sound that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance… this is the element of sounds – this is called "the element of sounds". ⤵ Therein, what is the ear-consciousness element? Depending on the ear and sounds there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding ear-consciousness element – this is called "the ear-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the nose element? The nose that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the nose element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of smells? The smell that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance… this is the element of smells – this is called "the element of smells". ⤵ Therein, what is the nose-consciousness element? Depending on the nose and smells there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding nose-consciousness element – this is called "the nose-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the tongue element? The tongue that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the tongue element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of tastes? The taste that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance… this is the element of tastes – this is called "the element of tastes". ⤵ Therein, what is the tongue-consciousness element? Depending on the tongue and tastes there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding tongue-consciousness element – this is called "the tongue-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the body element? The body that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the body element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of things touched? The earth element… this is the element of things touched – this is called "the element of things touched". ⤵ Therein, what is the body-consciousness element? Depending on the body and things touched there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding body-consciousness element – this is called "the body-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the mind element? Immediately after the arising and ceasing of the eye-consciousness element there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding mind element; immediately after the arising and ceasing of the ear-consciousness element… of the nose-consciousness element… of the tongue-consciousness element… of the body-consciousness element there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding mind element; or, at the first turning of attention towards any object whatever there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding mind element – this is called "the mind element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of mental objects? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the material form that is invisible and offers no resistance and is included in the sense-field of mental objects, and the unconditioned element. ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of feeling? As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is joined with contact. As a twofold class: there is feeling with a root cause, and feeling without one. As a threefold class: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, and neutral feeling… thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of feeling is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of feeling". ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of perception? As a single class, the aggregate of perception is joined with contact. As a twofold class: there is perception with a root cause, and perception without one. As a threefold class: there is wholesome perception, unwholesome perception, and neutral perception… thus the aggregate of perception is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of perception is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of perception". ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of mental formations? As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is joined with mind. As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes, and formations that are not. As a threefold class: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, and neutral formations… thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of mental formations". ⤵ Therein, what is the material form that is invisible, offers no resistance, and is included in the sense-field of mental objects? The faculty of femininity… physical food – this is called the material form that is "invisible, offers no resistance, and is included in the sense-field of mental objects". ⤵ Therein, what is the unconditioned element? The ending of desire, the ending of hatred, and the ending of delusion – this is called "the unconditioned element". This is called "the element of mental objects". ⤵ Therein, what is the mind-consciousness element? Immediately after the arising and ceasing of the eye-consciousness element there arises the mind element, and immediately after the arising and ceasing of the mind element there arises mind, mentality, mental activity… and the corresponding mind-consciousness element; immediately after the arising and ceasing of the ear-consciousness element… of the nose-consciousness element… of the tongue-consciousness element… of the body-consciousness element there arises the mind element, and immediately after the arising and ceasing of that mind element there arises mind, mentality, mental activity… and the corresponding mind-consciousness element; and depending on the mind and mental objects there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding mind-consciousness element – this is called "the mind-consciousness element".
The Classification According to the Abhidhamma is finished.

Tattha katamā kāmadhātu? Kāmapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā cetaso abhiniropanā micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati kāmadhātu. Heṭṭhato avīcinirayaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā uparito paranimmitavasavattī deve anto karitvā yaṃ etasmiṃ antare etthāvacarā ettha pariyāpannā khandhadhātuāyatanā rūpā [rūpaṃ (syā.)] vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "kāmadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā byāpādadhātu? Byāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "byāpādadhātu". Dasasu vā āghātavatthūsu cittassa āghāto paṭighāto paṭighaṃ paṭivirodho kopo pakopo sampakopo doso padoso sampadoso cittassa byāpatti manopadoso kodho kujjhanā kujjhitattaṃ doso dussanā dussitattaṃ byāpatti byāpajjanā virodho paṭivirodho caṇḍikkaṃ asuropo anattamanatā cittassa – ayaṃ vuccati "byāpādadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā vihiṃsādhātu? Vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… micchāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "vihiṃsādhātu". Idhekacco pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā rajjuyā vā aññataraññatarena satte viheṭheti, yā evarūpā heṭhanā viheṭhanā hiṃsanā vihiṃsanā rosanā virosanā parūpaghāto – ayaṃ vuccati "vihiṃsādhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā nekkhammadhātu? Nekkhammapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "nekkhammadhātu". Sabbepi kusalā dhammā "nekkhammadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā abyāpādadhātu? Abyāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko…pe… sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "abyāpādadhātu". Yā sattesu metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati "abyāpādadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā avihiṃsādhātu? Avihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā cetaso abhiniropanā sammāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati "avihiṃsādhātu" . Yā sattesu karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti – ayaṃ vuccati "avihiṃsādhātu".
Imā cha dhātuyo.
Iti imāni tīṇi chakkāni tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo honti.
Suttantabhājanīyaṃ.
2. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ

Aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo – cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu, saddadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānadhātu, gandhadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhādhātu, rasadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu , kāyadhātu, phoṭṭhabbadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu, dhammadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu.

Tattha katamā cakkhudhātu? Yaṃ cakkhu catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati "cakkhudhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā rūpadhātu? Yaṃ rūpaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya vaṇṇanibhā…pe… rūpadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati "rūpadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā cakkhuviññāṇadhātu? Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjācakkhuviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati "cakkhuviññāṇadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā sotadhātu? Yaṃ sotaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati "sotadhātu" . ⤵ Tattha katamā saddadhātu? Yo saddo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho…pe… saddadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati "saddadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā sotaviññāṇadhātu? Sotañca paṭicca sadde ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāsotaviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati "sotaviññāṇadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā ghānadhātu? Yaṃ ghānaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati "ghānadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā gandhadhātu? Yo gandho catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho…pe… gandhadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati "gandhadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā ghānaviññāṇadhātu? Ghānañca paṭicca gandhe ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāghānaviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati "ghānaviññāṇadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā jivhādhātu? Yā jivhā catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati "jivhādhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā rasadhātu? Yo raso catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya anidassano sappaṭigho…pe… rasadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati "rasadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā jivhāviññāṇadhātu? Jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjājivhāviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati "jivhāviññāṇadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā kāyadhātu? Yo kāyo catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo…pe… suñño gāmopeso – ayaṃ vuccati "kāyadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā phoṭṭhabbadhātu? Pathavīdhātu…pe… phoṭṭhabbadhātupesā – ayaṃ vuccati "phoṭṭhabbadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā kāyaviññāṇadhātu? Kāyañca paṭicca phoṭṭhabbe ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjākāyaviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati "kāyaviññāṇadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā manodhātu? Cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanodhātu; sotaviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanodhātu sabbadhammesu vā pana paṭhamasamannāhāro uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanodhātu – ayaṃ vuccati "manodhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā dhammadhātu? Vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu. ⤵ Tattha katamo vedanākkhandho? Ekavidhena vedanākkhandho – phassasampayutto . Duvidhena vedanākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Tividhena vedanākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena vedanākkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena vedanākkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati "vedanākkhandho". ⤵ Tattha katamo saññākkhandho? Ekavidhena saññākkhandho – phassasampayutto. Duvidhena saññākkhandho – atthi sahetuko, atthi ahetuko. Tividhena saññākkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena saññākkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena saññākkhandho. Ayaṃ vuccati "saññākkhandho". ⤵ Tattha katamo saṅkhārakkhandho? Ekavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – cittasampayutto. Duvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi hetu, atthi ahetu. Tividhena saṅkhārakkhandho – atthi kusalo, atthi akusalo, atthi abyākato…pe… evaṃ dasavidhena saṅkhārakkhandho…pe… evaṃ bahuvidhena saṅkhārakkhandho – ayaṃ vuccati "saṅkhārakkhandho". ⤵ Tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ? Itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro – idaṃ vuccati rūpaṃ "anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ". ⤵ Tattha katamā asaṅkhatā dhātu? Rāgakkhayo, dosakkhayo, mohakkhayo – ayaṃ vuccati "asaṅkhatā dhātu". Ayaṃ vuccati "dhammadhātu". ⤵ Tattha katamā manoviññāṇadhātu? Cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati manodhātu, manodhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu; sotaviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… ghānaviññāṇadhātuyā …pe… jivhāviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati manodhātu, manodhātuyāpi uppajjitvā niruddhasamanantarā uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ…pe… tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ hadayaṃ paṇḍaraṃ mano manāyatanaṃ manindriyaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandho tajjāmanoviññāṇadhātu – ayaṃ vuccati "manoviññāṇadhātu".
Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ.
3. The Section of Questions and Answers

There are eighteen elements – the eye element, the element of sights, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the element of sounds, the ear-consciousness element; the nose element, the element of smells, the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the element of tastes, the tongue-consciousness element; the body element, the element of things touched, the body-consciousness element; the mind element, the element of mental objects, and the mind-consciousness element.
Of the eighteen elements, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… how many involve conflict, how many are free from conflict?
1. The Triads

Sixteen elements are neutral. Two elements may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. Ten elements cannot be described as joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. Five elements are joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The body-consciousness element may be joined with pleasant feeling or with painful feeling. The mind-consciousness element may be joined with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The element of mental objects may be joined with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, or may not be describable as joined with any of these. ⤵ Ten elements are neither results nor things that produce results. Five elements are results. The mind element may be a result, or neither a result nor something that produces results. Two elements may be results, may produce results, or may be neither. ⤵ Ten elements are taken up at birth and able to be clung to. The element of sounds is not taken up but able to be clung to. Five elements may be taken up and able to be clung to, or not taken up but able to be clung to. Two elements may be taken up and able to be clung to, not taken up but able to be clung to, or neither taken up nor able to be clung to. ⤵ Sixteen elements are undefiled yet open to defilement. Two elements may be defiled and open to defilement, undefiled yet open to defilement, or neither defiled nor open to defilement. Fifteen elements are without thought and examination. The mind element has both thought and examination. The mind-consciousness element may have both thought and examination, examination only, or neither. The element of mental objects may have both thought and examination, examination only, or neither, or may not be describable as any of these. Ten elements cannot be described as accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity. Five elements are accompanied by equanimity. The body-consciousness element is not accompanied by joy; it may be accompanied by happiness or not; it is not accompanied by equanimity; or it may not be describable as "accompanied by happiness". Two elements may be accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity, or may not be describable as accompanied by any of these. ⤵ Sixteen elements are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Two elements may be abandoned by seeing, by development, or by neither. Sixteen elements have root causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Two elements may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing, root causes to be abandoned by development, or root causes to be abandoned by neither. Sixteen elements neither lead to further accumulation nor to dismantling. Two elements may lead to accumulation, to dismantling, or to neither. Sixteen elements belong neither to trainees nor to those beyond training. Two elements may belong to trainees, to those beyond training, or to neither. ⤵ Sixteen elements are limited. Two elements may be limited, expanded, or measureless. Ten elements have no object. Six elements have a limited object. Two elements may have a limited object, an expanded object, or a measureless object, or may not be describable as having any of these. Sixteen elements are middling. Two elements may be inferior, middling, or superior. Sixteen elements are not fixed in their outcome. Two elements may be fixed in wrongness, fixed in rightness, or not fixed. ⤵ Ten elements have no object. Six elements cannot be described as having the path as their object, the path as their cause, or the path as their dominant factor. Two elements may have the path as their object, the path as their cause, or the path as their dominant factor, or may not be describable as any of these. Ten elements may be arisen or bound to arise; they cannot be described as "not arisen". The element of sounds may be arisen or not arisen; it cannot be described as "bound to arise". Six elements may be arisen, not arisen, or bound to arise. The element of mental objects may be arisen, not arisen, or bound to arise, or may not be describable as any of these. ⤵ Seventeen elements may be past, future, or present. The element of mental objects may be past, future, or present, or may not be describable as past, future, or present. Ten elements have no object. Six elements have a present object. Two elements may have a past object, a future object, or a present object, or may not be describable as having any of these; they may be internal, external, or both internal and external. ⤵ Ten elements have no object. Six elements may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external. Two elements may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, or may not be describable as having any of these. The element of sights is visible and offers resistance. Nine elements are invisible and offer no resistance. Eight elements are invisible and offer no resistance.
3. Pañhāpucchakaṃ

Aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo – cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu, saddadhātu, sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānadhātu, gandhadhātu, ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhādhātu, rasadhātu, jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyadhātu, phoṭṭhabbadhātu, kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu, dhammadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu.
Aṭṭhārasannaṃ dhātūnaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā…pe… kati saraṇā, kati araṇā?
1. Tikaṃ

Soḷasa dhātuyo abyākatā. Dve dhātuyo siyā kusalā, siyā akusalā, siyā abyākatā. Dasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – "sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi. Pañca dhātuyo adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Kāyaviññāṇadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā. Dhammadhātu siyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, siyā na vattabbā – "sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi, "adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā"tipi. ⤵ Dasa dhātuyo nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Pañca dhātuyo vipākā. Manodhātu siyā vipākā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Dve dhātuyo siyā vipākā, siyā vipākadhammadhammā, siyā nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. ⤵ Dasa dhātuyo upādinnupādāniyā. Saddadhātu anupādinnupādāniyā. Pañca dhātuyo siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā. Dve dhātuyo siyā upādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnupādāniyā, siyā anupādinnaanupādāniyā. ⤵ Soḷasa dhātuyo asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā. Dve dhātuyo siyā saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, siyā asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā. Pannarasa dhātuyo avitakkaavicārā. Manodhātu savitakkasavicārā. Manoviññāṇadhātu siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā. Dhammadhātu siyā savitakkasavicārā, siyā avitakkavicāramattā, siyā avitakkaavicārā, siyā na vattabbā – "savitakkasavicārā"tipi, "avitakkavicāramattā"tipi, "avitakkaavicārā"tipi. Dasa dhātuyo na vattabbā – "pītisahagatā"tipi, "sukhasahagatā"tipi, "upekkhāsahagatā"tipi . Pañca dhātuyo upekkhāsahagatā. Kāyaviññāṇadhātu na pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, na upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā – "sukhasahagatā"ti. Dve dhātuyo siyā pītisahagatā, siyā sukhasahagatā, siyā upekkhāsahagatā, siyā na vattabbā – "pītisahagatā"tipi, "sukhasahagatā"tipi, "upekkhāsahagatā"tipi. ⤵ Soḷasa dhātuyo neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Dve dhātuyo siyā dassanena pahātabbā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Soḷasa dhātuyo neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Dve dhātuyo siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā, siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, siyā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā. Soḷasa dhātuyo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Dve dhātuyo siyā ācayagāmino, siyā apacayagāmino, siyā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino. Soḷasa dhātuyo nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Dve dhātuyo siyā sekkhā, siyā asekkhā, siyā nevasekkhanāsekkhā. ⤵ Soḷasa dhātuyo parittā. Dve dhātuyo siyā parittā, siyā mahaggatā, siyā appamāṇā. Dasa dhātuyo anārammaṇā. Cha dhātuyo parittārammaṇā. Dve dhātuyo siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā – "parittārammaṇā"tipi, "mahaggatārammaṇā"tipi, "appamāṇārammaṇā"tipi. Soḷasa dhātuyo majjhimā. Dve dhātuyo siyā hīnā, siyā majjhimā, siyā paṇītā. Soḷasa dhātuyo aniyatā. Dve dhātuyo siyā micchattaniyatā, siyā sammattaniyatā, siyā aniyatā. ⤵ Dasa dhātuyo anārammaṇā. Cha dhātuyo na vattabbā – "maggārammaṇā"tipi, "maggahetukā"tipi, "maggādhipatino"tipi. Dve dhātuyo siyā maggārammaṇā, siyā maggahetukā, siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā – "maggārammaṇā"tipi, "maggahetukā"tipi, "maggādhipatino"tipi. Dasa dhātuyo siyā uppannā, siyā uppādino, siyā na vattabbā – "anuppannā"ti. Saddadhātu siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā na vattabbā – "uppādinī"ti. Cha dhātuyo siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādino. Dhammadhātu siyā uppannā, siyā anuppannā, siyā uppādinī, siyā na vattabbā – "uppannā"tipi, "anuppannā"tipi, "uppādinī"tipi. ⤵ Sattarasa dhātuyo siyā atītā, siyā anāgatā, siyā paccuppannā. 4. Analysis of the Truths
1. Classification According to the Discourses

There are four noble truths – the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the ending of suffering, and the noble truth of the way leading to the ending of suffering.
1. The Truth of Suffering

Therein, what is the noble truth of suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair are suffering; association with what is disliked is suffering; separation from what is loved is suffering; not getting what one wants is also suffering; in brief, the five aggregates that are clung to are suffering.

Therein, what is birth? The birth of this or that being into this or that order of beings – the being born, the descent, the coming forth, the appearance of the aggregates, the acquiring of the sense-fields – this is called "birth".

Therein, what is aging? The aging of this or that being in this or that order of beings – the growing old, brokenness of teeth, greyness of hair, wrinkling of skin, the decline of the life span, the ripening of the faculties – this is called "aging".

Therein, what is death? The passing of this or that being from this or that order of beings – the passing away, the breaking up, the disappearance, mortality, death, the completion of one's time, the breaking up of the aggregates, the laying down of the body, the cutting off of the life faculty – this is called "death".

Therein, what is sorrow? When someone is touched by loss of relatives, loss of wealth, loss through illness, loss of virtue, or loss of view, when someone meets with one misfortune or another, is touched by one painful thing or another – the sorrow, the sorrowing, the state of sorrow, inner sorrow, deep inner sorrow, the burning of the mind, sadness, the dart of sorrow – this is called "sorrow".

Therein, what is lamentation? When someone is touched by loss of relatives, loss of wealth, loss through illness, loss of virtue, or loss of view, when someone meets with one misfortune or another, is touched by one painful thing or another – the crying out, the lamenting, the act of crying out, the act of lamenting, the state of crying out, the state of lamenting; the talk, the raving, the wailing; the moaning, the act of moaning, the state of moaning – this is called "lamentation".
Therein, what is pain? Bodily discomfort, bodily pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of body-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of body-contact – this is called "pain".

Therein, what is sadness? Mental discomfort, mental pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of mind-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "sadness".

Therein, what is despair? When someone is touched by loss of relatives, loss of wealth, loss through illness, loss of virtue, or loss of view, when someone meets with one misfortune or another, is touched by one painful thing or another – the distress, the despair, the state of distress, the state of despair – this is called "despair".

Therein, what is the suffering of association with what is disliked? Here, whatever sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and things touched are unwanted, unattractive, and disagreeable to someone, or whoever wishes them ill, wishes them harm, wishes them discomfort, wishes them no security – meeting, coming together, joining, and mingling with these – this is called "the suffering of association with what is disliked".

Therein, what is the suffering of separation from what is loved? Here, whatever sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and things touched are wanted, attractive, and agreeable to someone, or whoever wishes them well, wishes them good, wishes them comfort, wishes them security – mother or father, brother or sister, friends or companions, relatives or kin – not meeting, not coming together, not joining, and not mingling with these – this is called "the suffering of separation from what is loved".

Therein, what is "not getting what one wants is also suffering"? In beings subject to birth such a wish arises: "Oh, that we were not subject to birth! Oh, that birth would not come to us!" But this cannot be gained by wishing. This too is "not getting what one wants is also suffering". ⤵ In beings subject to aging… in beings subject to illness… in beings subject to death… in beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair such a wish arises: "Oh, that we were not subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair! Oh, that sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair would not come to us!" But this cannot be gained by wishing. This too is "not getting what one wants is also suffering".

Therein, what is "in brief, the five aggregates that are clung to are suffering"? Namely: the aggregate of material form that is clung to, the aggregate of feeling that is clung to, the aggregate of perception that is clung to, the aggregate of mental formations that is clung to, and the aggregate of consciousness that is clung to. These are called "in brief, the five aggregates that are clung to are suffering". ⤵ This is called "the noble truth of suffering".
2. The Truth of the Origin

Therein, what is the noble truth of the origin of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and desire, delighting now here, now there – namely: craving for sense pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence. ⤵ Now where does this craving arise when it arises? Where does it settle when it settles? Whatever in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing – there this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ And what in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing? The eye in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. The ear in the world… the nose in the world… the tongue in the world… the body in the world… the mind in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ Sights in the world are a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Sounds in the world… smells in the world… tastes in the world… things touched in the world… mental objects in the world are a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ Eye-consciousness in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Ear-consciousness in the world… nose-consciousness in the world… tongue-consciousness in the world… body-consciousness in the world… mind-consciousness in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ Eye-contact in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Ear-contact in the world… nose-contact in the world… tongue-contact in the world… body-contact in the world… mind-contact in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ Feeling born of eye-contact in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Feeling born of ear-contact in the world… feeling born of nose-contact in the world… feeling born of tongue-contact in the world… feeling born of body-contact in the world… feeling born of mind-contact in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ Perception of sights in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Perception of sounds in the world… perception of smells in the world… perception of tastes in the world… perception of things touched in the world… perception of mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ Intention regarding sights in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Intention regarding sounds in the world… intention regarding smells in the world… intention regarding tastes in the world… intention regarding things touched in the world… intention regarding mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ Craving for sights in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Craving for sounds in the world… craving for smells in the world… craving for tastes in the world… craving for things touched in the world… craving for mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ Thought about sights in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Thought about sounds in the world… thought about smells in the world… thought about tastes in the world… thought about things touched in the world… thought about mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ Examination of sights in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Examination of sounds in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Examination of smells in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Examination of tastes in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Examination of things touched in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. Examination of mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving arises when it arises; there it settles when it settles. ⤵ This is called "the noble truth of the origin of suffering".
4. Saccavibhaṅgo
1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ
Cattāri ariyasaccāni – dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ [dukkhasamudayo (syā.)] ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ [dukkhanirodho (syā.)] ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ.
1. Dukkhasaccaṃ

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Jātipi dukkhā, jarāpi dukkhā, maraṇampi dukkhaṃ, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsāpi dukkhā, appiyehi sampayogo dukkho, piyehi vippayogo dukkho, yaṃ picchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ, saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā.
Tattha katamā jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jāti sañjāti okkanti abhinibbatti khandhānaṃ pātubhāvo āyatanānaṃ paṭilābho – ayaṃ vuccati "jāti".
Tattha katamā jarā? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṃ pāliccaṃ valittacatā āyuno saṃhāni indriyānaṃ paripāko – ayaṃ vuccati "jarā".

Tattha katamaṃ maraṇaṃ? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṃ maccu maraṇaṃ kālakiriyā khandhānaṃ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo jīvitindriyassupacchedo – idaṃ vuccati "maraṇaṃ".

Tattha katamo soko? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa soko socanā socitattaṃ antosoko antoparisoko cetaso parijjhāyanā domanassaṃ sokasallaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "soko".

Tattha katamo paridevo? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa ādevo paridevo ādevanā paridevanā ādevitattaṃ paridevitattaṃ vācā palāpo vippalāpo lālappo lālappanā lālappitattaṃ [lālapo lālapanā lālapitattaṃ (syā.)] – ayaṃ vuccati "paridevo".
Tattha katamaṃ dukkhaṃ? Yaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ kāyasamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "dukkhaṃ".
Tattha katamaṃ domanassaṃ? Yaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetosamphassajaṃ asātaṃ dukkhaṃ vedayitaṃ cetosamphassajā asātā dukkhā vedanā – idaṃ vuccati "domanassaṃ".

Tattha katamo upāyāso? Ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa sīlabyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa diṭṭhibyasanena vā phuṭṭhassa aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa āyāso upāyāso āyāsitattaṃ upāyāsitattaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati "upāyāso".

Tattha katamo appiyehi sampayogo dukkho? Idha yassa te honti aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā rūpā saddā gandhā rasā phoṭṭhabbā, ye vā panassa te honti anatthakāmā ahitakāmā aphāsukakāmā ayogakkhemakāmā; yā tehi saṅgati samāgamo samodhānaṃ missībhāvo – ayaṃ vuccati "appiyehi sampayogo dukkho".

Tattha katamo piyehi vippayogo dukkho? Idha yassa te honti iṭṭhā kantā manāpā rūpā saddā gandhā rasā phoṭṭhabbā, ye vā panassa te honti atthakāmā hitakāmā phāsukakāmā yogakkhemakāmā mātā vā pitā vā bhātā vā bhaginī vā mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā; yā tehi asaṅgati asamāgamo asamodhānaṃ amissībhāvo – ayaṃ vuccati "piyehi vippayogo dukkho".

Tattha katamaṃ yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ? Jātidhammānaṃ sattānaṃ evaṃ icchā uppajjati – "aho vata, mayaṃ na jātidhammā assāma; na ca, vata, no jāti āgaccheyyā"ti! Na kho panetaṃ icchāya pattabbaṃ. Idampi "yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ". ⤵ Jarādhammānaṃ sattānaṃ…pe… byādhidhammānaṃ sattānaṃ…pe… maraṇadhammānaṃ sattānaṃ…pe… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammānaṃ sattānaṃ evaṃ icchā uppajjati – "aho vata, mayaṃ na sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā assāma; na ca, vata, no sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā āgaccheyyu"nti! Na kho panetaṃ icchāya pattabbaṃ. Idampi "yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ".

Tattha katame saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā? Seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime vuccanti "saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā". ⤵ Idaṃ vuccati "dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ".
2. Samudayasaccaṃ

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobhavikā [ponobbhavikā (syā. ka.)] nandirāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā. ⤵ Sā kho panesā taṇhā kattha uppajjamānā uppajjati, kattha nivisamānā nivisati? Yaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ, etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Kiñca loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ? Cakkhuṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Sotaṃ loke…pe… ghānaṃ loke… jivhā loke… kāyo loke… mano loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Rūpā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddā loke…pe… gandhā loke… rasā loke… phoṭṭhabbā loke… dhammā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Sotaviññāṇaṃ loke…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ loke… jivhāviññāṇaṃ loke… kāyaviññāṇaṃ loke… manoviññāṇaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Cakkhusamphasso loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Sotasamphasso loke…pe… ghānasamphasso loke… jivhāsamphasso loke… kāyasamphasso loke… manosamphasso loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Cakkhusamphassajā vedanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Sotasamphassajā vedanā loke…pe… ghānasamphassajā vedanā loke… jivhāsamphassajā vedanā loke… kāyasamphassajā vedanā loke… manosamphassajā vedanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Rūpasaññā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddasaññā loke…pe… gandhasaññā loke… rasasaññā loke… phoṭṭhabbasaññā loke… dhammasaññā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Rūpasañcetanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddasañcetanā loke…pe… gandhasañcetanā loke… rasasañcetanā loke… phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā loke… dhammasañcetanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Rūpataṇhā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddataṇhā loke…pe… gandhataṇhā loke… rasataṇhā loke… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā loke… dhammataṇhā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Rūpavitakko loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati . Saddavitakko loke…pe… gandhavitakko loke… rasavitakko loke… phoṭṭhabbavitakko loke… dhammavitakko loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Rūpavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Saddavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati , ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Gandhavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Rasavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Phoṭṭhabbavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Dhammavicāro loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. ⤵ Idaṃ vuccati "dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ".
3. The Truth of the Ending

Therein, what is the noble truth of the ending of suffering? It is the complete fading away and ending of that same craving – giving it up, letting it go, release from it, not relying on it. ⤵ Now where is this craving abandoned when it is abandoned? Where does it cease when it ceases? Whatever in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing – there this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ And what in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing? The eye in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. The ear in the world… the nose in the world… the tongue in the world… the body in the world… the mind in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ Sights in the world are a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. Sounds in the world… smells in the world… tastes in the world… things touched in the world… mental objects in the world are a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ Eye-consciousness in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. Ear-consciousness in the world… nose-consciousness in the world… tongue-consciousness in the world… body-consciousness in the world… mind-consciousness in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ Eye-contact in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. Ear-contact in the world… nose-contact in the world… tongue-contact in the world… body-contact in the world… mind-contact in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ Feeling born of eye-contact in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. Feeling born of ear-contact in the world… feeling born of nose-contact in the world… feeling born of tongue-contact in the world… feeling born of body-contact in the world… feeling born of mind-contact in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ Perception of sights in the world… perception of sounds in the world… perception of smells in the world… perception of tastes in the world… perception of things touched in the world… perception of mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ Intention regarding sights in the world… intention regarding sounds in the world… intention regarding smells in the world… intention regarding tastes in the world… intention regarding things touched in the world… intention regarding mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ Craving for sights in the world… craving for sounds in the world… craving for smells in the world… craving for tastes in the world… craving for things touched in the world… craving for mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ Thought about sights in the world… thought about sounds in the world… thought about smells in the world… thought about tastes in the world… thought about things touched in the world… thought about mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ Examination of sights in the world… examination of sounds in the world… examination of smells in the world… examination of tastes in the world… examination of things touched in the world… examination of mental objects in the world is a lovely thing, a pleasing thing. There this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned; there it ceases when it ceases. ⤵ This is called "the noble truth of the ending of suffering".
4. The Truth of the Path

Therein, what is the noble truth of the way leading to the ending of suffering? It is just this noble eightfold path, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. ⤵ Therein, what is right view? Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the ending of suffering, knowledge of the way leading to the ending of suffering – this is called "right view". ⤵ Therein, what is right intention? The intention of renunciation, the intention of goodwill, the intention of harmlessness – this is called "right intention". ⤵ Therein, what is right speech? Refraining from false speech, refraining from divisive speech, refraining from harsh speech, refraining from idle chatter – this is called "right speech". ⤵ Therein, what is right action? Refraining from killing living beings, refraining from taking what is not given, refraining from sexual misconduct – this is called "right action". ⤵ Therein, what is right livelihood? Here a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, makes a living by right livelihood – this is called "right livelihood". ⤵ Therein, what is right effort? Here a monk generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies the mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of bad, unwholesome states that have not yet arisen. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies the mind, and endeavours for the abandoning of bad, unwholesome states that have arisen. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies the mind, and endeavours for the arising of wholesome states that have not yet arisen. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies the mind, and endeavours for the maintaining, non-confusion, increase, expansion, development, and fulfilment of wholesome states that have arisen. This is called "right effort". ⤵ Therein, what is right mindfulness? Here a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body – ardent, clearly understanding, and mindful, having put away covetousness and sadness towards the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings… the mind in the mind… mental objects in mental objects – ardent, clearly understanding, and mindful, having put away covetousness and sadness towards the world. This is called "right mindfulness". ⤵ Therein, what is right concentration? Here a monk, secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, which has thought and examination and the joy and happiness born of seclusion. With the stilling of thought and examination, he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, which has inner confidence and unification of mind, is without thought and examination, and has the joy and happiness born of concentration. With the fading away of joy, he dwells with equanimity, mindful and clearly understanding, and experiences happiness with the body; he enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption, of which the noble ones declare: "Equanimous and mindful, one dwells happily." With the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain, and with the earlier disappearance of gladness and sadness, he enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption, which is neither painful nor pleasant and has purity of mindfulness through equanimity. This is called "right concentration". ⤵ This is called "the noble truth of the way leading to the ending of suffering".
The Classification According to the Discourses is finished.
2. Classification According to the Abhidhamma

There are four truths – suffering, the origin of suffering, the ending of suffering, and the way leading to the ending of suffering. ⤵ Therein, what is the origin of suffering? Craving – this is called "the origin of suffering". ⤵ Therein, what is suffering? The remaining defilements, the remaining unwholesome states, the three wholesome roots that are subject to the mental taints, the remaining wholesome states subject to the taints, the results of wholesome and unwholesome states subject to the taints, the states that are mere functioning – neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the results of action – and all material form – this is called "suffering". ⤵ Therein, what is the ending of suffering? The abandoning of craving – this is called "the ending of suffering". ⤵ Therein, what is the way leading to the ending of suffering? Here, on an occasion when a monk develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out of the round, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage – secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, the way being difficult and direct knowledge slow – on that occasion there is the eightfold path: right view… right concentration. ⤵ Therein, what is right view? The wisdom, the understanding… the non-delusion, the investigation of states, the right view, the awakening factor of investigation of states that is a path factor, included in the path – this is called "right view". ⤵ Therein, what is right intention? The thinking, the thought… the right intention that is a path factor, included in the path – this is called "right intention". ⤵ Therein, what is right speech? The desisting, refraining, abstaining, and keeping away from the four kinds of verbal misconduct – the not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, the destroying of the causeway – the right speech that is a path factor, included in the path – this is called "right speech". ⤵ Therein, what is right action? The desisting, refraining, abstaining, and keeping away from the three kinds of bodily misconduct – the not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, the destroying of the causeway – the right action that is a path factor, included in the path – this is called "right action". ⤵ Therein, what is right livelihood? The desisting, refraining, abstaining, and keeping away from wrong livelihood – the not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, the destroying of the causeway – the right livelihood that is a path factor, included in the path – this is called "right livelihood". ⤵ Therein, what is right effort? The mental arousing of energy… the right effort, the awakening factor of energy that is a path factor, included in the path – this is called "right effort". ⤵ Therein, what is right mindfulness? The mindfulness, the remembering… the right mindfulness, the awakening factor of mindfulness that is a path factor, included in the path – this is called "right mindfulness". ⤵ Therein, what is right concentration? The steadiness of mind, the stability… the right concentration, the awakening factor of concentration that is a path factor, included in the path – this is called "right concentration". This is called "the way leading to the ending of suffering". The remaining states are associated with the way leading to the ending of suffering.
3. Nirodhasaccaṃ

Tattha katamaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo. ⤵ Sā kho panesā taṇhā kattha pahīyamānā pahīyati, kattha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati? Sotasamphasso loke…pe… ghānasamphasso loke… jivhāsamphasso loke… kāyasamphasso loke… manosamphasso loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Sotasamphassajā vedanā loke…pe… ghānasamphassajā vedanā loke… jivhāsamphassajā vedanā loke… kāyasamphassajā vedanā loke… manosamphassajā vedanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati. ⤵ Rūpasaññā loke… saddasaññā loke… gandhasaññā loke… rasasaññā loke… phoṭṭhabbasaññā loke… dhammasaññā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ. Etthesā taṇhā pahīyamānā pahīyati, ettha nirujjhamānā nirujjhati. ⤵ Rūpasañcetanā loke… saddasañcetanā loke… gandhasañcetanā loke… rasasañcetanā loke… phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā loke… dhammasañcetanā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ.
